**The “Concept only” popup is removed.** I saved the change and verified it; no dimensions or geometry changed.

For the cross bench, **12 mm plywood with reinforcement only where needed is a sensible starting point to compare against 9 mm construction.** The examples don’t support assuming 19 mm throughout.

These are documented approaches, rather than one universal camper-building standard:

| Approach | Actual example | Relevance to your bench |
|---|---|---|
| **12 mm birch plywood construction** | [Simple Camper Vans](https://www.simplecampervans.com/shop/conversion-modules/peugeot-partner-camper-van-conversion/) uses it for its Peugeot Partner microcamper seating/bed module. | Direct precedent for compact furniture whose panels form the structure. |
| **15 mm lightweight poplar plywood** | [Trekvana](https://www.trekvanacampers.ie/) specifies it for its furniture set, including a sliding bed and bench. | A thicker panel can still be relatively light because of the plywood species. |
| **9 mm plywood with reinforcement and thinner internal panels** | [This builder’s construction account](https://pperratt.weebly.com/the-van-plan---part-6.html) describes 9 mm structural panels, 5 mm internal panels, longitudinal reinforcement and shelves tying the furniture together. | Shows the thinner-panel approach, although this example is cabinetry rather than proof of a particular bed’s capacity. |

**Thickness alone is a poor guide to weight.** From published material data:

- **12 mm poplar:** approximately **5.0–5.8 kg/m²**.
- **9 mm birch:** approximately **6.1 kg/m²**.
- **12 mm birch:** approximately **8.2 kg/m²**.

Those are unfinished-panel figures derived from [Garnica’s poplar density](https://www.garnica.one/uploads/ea864e77-70b5-4505-a372-c717da786085/ea864e77-70b5-4505-a372-c717da786085.pdf) and [Metsä’s birch specifications](https://www.metsagroup.com/contentassets/8a5519dc6e534fcfa99c06759fbb8bad/metsa_wood_birch_plywood_product_datasheets_en.pdf). They are weight comparisons, not equivalent strength ratings.

For **maximum storage**, I would investigate making the vertical plywood walls do useful structural work: carry the slat supports down to the floor and brace the bench against sideways movement. Add small reinforcement strips or blocks at the sliding guides, toilet runners, joints and mounting points as required.

A full internal frame can defeat the benefit of thinner panels. For example, across the bench’s **580 mm dimension**:

- Two **12 mm walls** leave **556 mm** between them.
- Two **9 mm walls with 25 mm battens projecting inward** leave **512 mm at those battens**.

That’s a **44 mm difference at the opening**, despite using thinner plywood. Local battens don’t necessarily reduce the entire storage volume, but their position matters for getting the toilet and storage boxes through.

My proposed comparison for our design is:

| Component | Starting point to investigate |
|---|---|
| Main vertical bench walls | **12 mm lightweight plywood**, with supported edges and local reinforcement |
| Alternative wall construction | **9 mm plywood**, adding only the reinforcement the loads and joints require |
| Non-load-bearing closure panels | Thinner material selected for their span and hinges |
| Existing bed slats | Your **80 × 19 mm timber** |
| Slotted moving plywood comb | Size separately; the proposed **19 mm** is not a requirement for the surrounding box |

**I’d compare the complete weight and clear storage opening of those two wall constructions before choosing.** A 9 mm panel saves material, but only wins overall if its additional framing doesn’t consume that saving—or the storage space. The moving comb and occupied toilet runner attachments need their own load checks; they shouldn’t dictate the thickness of every panel.

**Yes, 7 mm plywood could be a valid choice. I haven’t established 12 mm as a minimum.** “Supported edges” was too vague: it matters whether the supports simply keep a panel straight or carry the bed’s weight themselves.

For our cross bench, here are two concrete constructions to compare. These are proposed arrangements, not load-checked cutting plans.

**1. A 12 mm plywood wall that carries the load**

For each long vertical side of the cross bench:

- Its **bottom edge bears on the floor**.
- Its wall-side end joins the perpendicular end panel, forming a stiff corner. A **20 × 20 mm glued corner cleat** is one possible joint.
- A **40 mm-wide plywood reinforcement strip**, bonded along the top inside face, provides more material where the bed supports or guides attach.
- The open end gets a local reinforcement strip if required around the guide attachment.

Here, the plywood wall carries load from the bed supports down to the floor. The corner and strips restrain movement and strengthen connections; they aren’t a complete frame replacing the wall’s structural role.

You could substitute 7 mm, but then we must check the thinner panel’s tendency to bow and the concentrated loads at the guides. Supporting its perimeter doesn’t automatically prevent its middle from flexing.

**2. A 7 mm wall with bonded plywood reinforcement**

This is the lighter option I’d investigate for your priorities:

- **7 mm plywood for the main panel.**
- **50 mm-wide strips of another 7 mm layer**, bonded flat around its inside perimeter.
- That makes it **14 mm thick at the edges, 7 mm through the middle**.
- Add reinforcement at runner attachments, positioned to carry their loads into the reinforced edges.
- Tie the two sides together with the wall-side end panel and the necessary bed supports.

This avoids a bulky timber skeleton. The strips must be properly bonded over their faces to act together; a few screws joining loose layers wouldn’t give the same result. [WEST SYSTEM’s structural bonding guidance](https://www.westsystem.com/instruction/epoxy-basics/bonding-and-clamping/) explains that distinction.

For an illustrative **870 × 381 mm side panel**, using the same assumed plywood density of 450 kg/m³:

| Panel construction | Approximate plywood weight |
|---|---:|
| Plain 12 mm panel | 1.79 kg |
| 7 mm panel with a 50 mm-wide, 7 mm perimeter doubler | 1.41 kg |

That excludes glue, fittings and any additional reinforcement. It shows a potential saving, **not proof that the two panels have equal capacity**.

A third possibility is **7 mm cladding on a complete post-and-rail frame**. In that arrangement the frame carries the bed, so there is much less reason to use thick cladding—but the frame’s weight and intrusion into storage must be counted.

**For maximum storage and lightness, I’d investigate the locally reinforced 7 mm construction alongside the 12 mm structural-wall option.** The next useful step is to place the sliding guides and toilet runners: their loads and attachment positions should determine where reinforcement goes.

**Yes—this is a sensible way to investigate a light, space-efficient bench.** A continuous 7 mm panel with a second, inverted-U-shaped 7 mm layer bonded behind it gives you **14 mm along the top and down both ends**, while keeping the middle thin.

The two layers do complementary jobs:

- **The reinforced top band** receives the slat supports and distributes their loads toward the ends.
- **The reinforced vertical ends** continue down to the floor, providing a direct route for those loads.
- **The intact 7 mm centre** helps prevent the panel distorting sideways. It contributes structurally too.

For your roughly **870 × 400 mm panel**, I would make the reinforcement as one continuous piece, with **rounded inside corners** where its top band meets its legs. Keep both legs flush with the panel’s bottom so they actually bear on the base beneath them.

The main dimension to work out next is **how deep that top band should be**, followed by the width of the two legs. “14 mm thick” alone doesn’t establish its capacity: a shallow strip and a deep band behave very differently. Runner attachments and connections to the other bench panels also need deliberate positioning; small local blocks may be useful there without adding a full timber frame.

**Full-face bonding is essential.** Properly laminated plywood layers can act together; epoxy needs sound, prepared surfaces, complete contact and enough clamping to close gaps without squeezing the joint dry. That follows [WEST SYSTEM’s bonding guidance](https://www.westsystem.com/instruction/epoxy-basics/bonding-and-clamping/). If laser-cut, remove char wherever an edge will be bonded.

This deserves developing ahead of a bulky internal frame: it adds only **7 mm of inward projection at the reinforcement**. I’d carry it forward as the candidate construction, then size the bands around the actual plywood grade, slat supports and intended load—rather than assume the thickness alone proves sufficient strength.

>

**We can get a useful design with simple hand calculations and a physical prototype. FEA isn’t necessary at this stage.** The calculation needs to follow how the load reaches the floor, rather than picking plywood thickness in isolation.

One refinement to my previous answer: **your intact 7 mm panel also carries vertical load if its bottom edge rests on the floor.** The reinforced arch isn’t working alone. A toilet opening or unsupported bottom edge would change that substantially.

For sizing, we check four things:

| Check | What it determines |
|---|---|
| Bending and sag of the top supports | Reinforcement depth and distance between supports |
| Compression and buckling of the sides | Width of the reinforced legs and how the panels are braced |
| Slats and sliding extension | Their unsupported span in both positions |
| Connections | Bond area, attachment positions and local reinforcement |

**The most useful rule of thumb is: increase the vertical depth of a support before adding thickness.** For a rectangular beam of the same material:

- Double its thickness: approximately twice the bending strength and stiffness.
- Double its vertical depth: approximately **four times the bending strength and eight times the stiffness**.
- Shorten its unsupported span: substantially less bending and sag.

Here is a worked example to show what that means—not a load rating for your bench.

Imagine the reinforced top band acting alone as a straight beam, supported at its ends:

- Span: **870 mm**.
- Combined thickness: **14 mm**.
- Load at its centre: **1,000 N**, approximately the weight of 102 kg, applied to this one support.
- Assumed stiffness: **6,000 N/mm²**, purely an illustrative material value.

| Top band’s vertical depth | Calculated bending stress | Calculated bending sag |
|---|---:|---:|
| 50 mm | 37.3 MPa | 15.7 mm |
| 75 mm | 16.6 MPa | 4.6 mm |
| 100 mm | 9.3 MPa | 2.0 mm |

The beam formulas are:

$$
\text{Stress}=\frac{3PL}{2th^2},
\qquad
\text{Bending sag}=\frac{PL^3}{4Eth^3}
$$

Here, $P$ is load, $L$ span, $t$ thickness, $h$ band depth and $E$ material stiffness.

**That table demonstrates the benefit of depth; it doesn’t establish that 100 mm is sufficient.** It ignores your central panel’s contribution, and excludes shear deformation, buckling and connection movement. We must compare the calculated stress with a suitable design strength for the actual plywood.

Plywood properties depend on grade, veneer arrangement and direction. Published breaking-strength values also require reductions before use as design limits; CHH explains this in its [Ecoply design guidance](https://chhply.co.nz/assets/Uploads/EcoplySpecificationInstallationGuideCurrent.pdf). For your upright reinforcement, we need properties appropriate to loading **within the plane of the sheet**, rather than blindly using a shelf-bending table.

My proposed approach is to calculate the loaded edge and extended mechanism first, retain the continuous thin panels where useful, and then test the assembled prototype with controlled weights while measuring movement. That lets us pursue lightness without guessing.

**What maximum combined occupant weight should we design for, and do you have a particular 7 mm plywood product in mind?** Those two inputs will let us turn this into actual proposed dimensions.

**Generally, yes—good-quality all-birch plywood is usually stronger and stiffer at the same thickness.** But “poplar on pine” isn’t a strength grade, so we need the particular product to make a reliable comparison.

Two distinctions matter:

- **All-birch versus birch-faced:** a thin birch face over another core does not give you the properties of all-birch plywood.
- **Strength versus weight:** birch is heavier. For example, Metsä’s birch is about **680 kg/m³**, while Garnica’s all-poplar plywood is **420–480 kg/m³**. Those figures describe those products—not your unidentified poplar/pine sheet. [Metsä data](https://www.metsagroup.com/contentassets/3a00acbdd0da4a3eba069dc6568bc7c9/metsa_wood_sp_product_datasheet_en.pdf), [Garnica data](https://www.garnica.one/uploads/ea864e77-70b5-4505-a372-c717da786085/ea864e77-70b5-4505-a372-c717da786085.pdf).

For your bench, **birch reinforcement bonded to a lighter plywood side panel is an option worth comparing**. It could put the stronger material around the top and ends without paying its weight penalty across the whole panel. Whether that saves weight overall depends on the dimensions each material needs.

**Do you have a link to the “poplar on pine” plywood?** Its core construction and published properties will tell us more than the face species.

**Yes—we should include the slats, mattress and bedding, plus an allowance for movement.** Your **170 kg of occupants** is the starting load, not the complete design load.

For our preliminary calculations, I suggest:

| Load case | Proposed approach |
|---|---|
| Sleeping normally | 170 kg occupants + actual supported weight of slats, mattress and bedding |
| Vigorous movement | Initially check **twice the occupants’ static weight**, plus the supported materials |
| Sitting or kneeling near an edge | Apply the person’s load locally, rather than spreading it across the whole bed |
| Both people on the cross bench | Check that bench for both occupants together |
| Sideways movement | Check panel bracing, joints, extension guides and legs against sideways distortion |

The **2× movement allowance is a preliminary engineering assumption**, not a bed-standard requirement or a guarantee against every impact. A hard landing can exceed it, and repeated movement can loosen joints even when nothing breaks. Bed testing therefore includes separate static, impact and horizontal-load checks. [SATRA’s explanation of EN 1725](https://www.satra.com/spotlight/article.php?id=566)

For illustration, **if** the supported materials weighed 30 kg:

- Normal load: **170 + 30 = 200 kg**, approximately **2.0 kN**.
- Preliminary movement case: **2 × 170 + 30 = 370 kg equivalent**, approximately **3.6 kN**.

That does **not** mean every panel must support 370 kg individually. We calculate what reaches each support—but we must also check awkward positions, particularly someone sitting on the extended edge. This is how we avoid adding unnecessary material everywhere.

The movement allowance also **doesn’t replace the reductions used when calculating timber’s allowable strength**. They address different uncertainties.

One material correction from the documentation I found: IBuilt’s July 2024 sheet describes this CD range as **pine faces over a eucalyptus core**, with the 7 mm product rated **F8/F11**. **Yes—this is a useful simplification. We can design one standard reinforced panel, with a common top-band depth and a maximum distance between uprights.** Then use one opening for the cross bench and two for the long bench.

A point load halfway between supports produces the greatest **bending** for a given total vertical load on a simply supported beam. Loads near a support can instead govern crushing, shear or the connection. So we can keep one simple model and move the load along it.

**I suggest two load settings:**

| Calculation case | Concentrated vertical load | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| One person sitting heavily on the edge | **2,000 N — about 204 kg equivalent** | Exceeds twice one occupant’s 85 kg static weight |
| Common panel sized for both occupants | **4,000 N — about 408 kg equivalent** | Covers twice the combined occupant weight, with roughly 68 kg equivalent remaining for supported materials |

**Use 4,000 N as the demanding case if you want one common panel specification.** Putting that entire force into one point on one panel is deliberately conservative: it avoids relying on the mattress or neighbouring panels to distribute it.

That is our proposed calculation load, **not a certified capacity or a guarantee against jumping or every impact**. Bed standards separately test static loads, impact and repeated movement. [SATRA’s explanation](https://www.satra.com/spotlight/article.php?id=566)

The simplified model would be:

- A **400 mm-high, 7 mm-thick sheet**.
- A second **7 mm inverted-U reinforcement**, bonded over its full contact area.
- Reinforced uprights bearing directly on the floor.
- The top band treated as a beam between uprights.
- Initially ignore the thin central sheet’s contribution to carrying vertical load. Retain it physically—it can help brace the assembly.
- Assume the installed panel is restrained against falling or buckling sideways by its connections to the rest of the bench.

That last assumption matters: an upright plywood panel standing on its own is not equivalent to a panel securely joined into a box.

**Use a common maximum spacing, rather than identical openings.** For example, with *provisional* 75 mm-wide uprights:

| Panel | Reinforcement arrangement | Clear opening width | Span between upright centres |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Cross bench, 870 mm wide | Two end uprights: inverted U | 720 mm | **795 mm** |
| Long bench, 1,280 mm long | End uprights plus centre upright: squared-off “m” | Two × 527.5 mm | **Two × 602.5 mm** |

An **800 mm maximum support-centre spacing** therefore accommodates both. The cross bench governs the common top-band size. A middle upright is only a support if it actually reaches and bears on the floor.

There is one important correction to the earlier illustrative calculations: **14 mm of plywood cannot be treated as 14 mm of wood with all its grain running along the beam.** The plywood design method accounts for the veneers running in each direction. IBuilt identifies the selected 7 mm product as five-ply, rated F8/F11, but its short product sheet does not provide the complete veneer thickness schedule. [IBuilt specification](https://nzwoodproducts.co.nz/media/products/files/2024/PJC0434-NZWood-IBuild_Structural_Plywood-Product_information_sheet-BPIR-v1.pdf), [EWPAA design guide, sections 5.3–5.8](https://www.plywoodandpanel.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/EWPAA-Structural-Plywood-LVL-Design-Guide-v5-FINAL-1.pdf)

To illustrate the likely scale, I calculated the **4,000 N load over an 800 mm span**, provisionally counting 7 mm of the laminated thickness as effective along the beam and using F8 stiffness:

| Top-band depth | Calculated bending stress | Approximate bending + shear deflection |
|---|---:|---:|
| 150 mm | 30.5 MPa | 3.4 mm |
| 200 mm | 17.1 MPa | 1.8 mm |
| 250 mm | 11.0 MPa | 1.1 mm |

**These are sensitivity results, not approved sizes:** that effective thickness remains an assumption, and allowable strength must account for material variability, moisture and stability. They show why a narrow 50–75 mm top strip should not be our starting assumption for this demanding case.

The remaining checks are specific and manageable:

- **Load entry:** the slat support must transfer force into both bonded layers without twisting the panel.
- **Uprights and floor contact:** check compression, sideways buckling and bearing; 75 mm is a trial width.
- **Inside corners and bond:** use rounded transitions and check the force transfer around them.
- **Repeated movement:** check that joints remain tight and the extension cannot disengage.

My recommendation is to explore **800 mm maximum spacing with a 200–250 mm top band**, alongside a **shorter-spacing alternative** that permits a shallower band. The extra reinforcement still projects only 7 mm into storage. This gives us a consistent, adjustable design model without pretending that the first beam calculation proves the complete bench.

**The revised calculation supports pursuing a thin panel with modest reinforcement. My proposed starting detail is a 50 mm top band and 50 mm end strips—not a deep beam.** That is a prototype dimension, not a calculated minimum.

The crucial condition is that **the complete bottom edge rests on the floor**, and the panel is held against sideways movement at its top and bottom.

For the **870 × 400 × 7 mm cross-bench panel**, the agreed load gives:

| Quantity | Result |
|---|---:|
| Total applied load | **1,471 N** — 150 kg |
| Loaded length along the top | **400 mm** |
| Average compression through the 7 mm sheet beneath it | **0.53 MPa** |

The load can travel down through that 400 mm-wide portion of the sheet. It does **not** need to travel sideways through the top strip to the two reinforced ends.

I also checked an idealised sideways-buckling case. IBuilt identifies this plywood as **7-8-5**: nominally 7 mm thick, five veneers, with 0.8 mm face veneers. For this calculation, I oriented the **face grain vertically** and counted only those two face veneers, omitting any helpful contribution from the inner veneers and reinforcement. Using the lower F8 stiffness:

- Compression in the counted veneers: **2.30 MPa**.
- Ideal elastic buckling load for the loaded strip: approximately **3.47 kN**, compared with the applied **1.47 kN**.

This is a useful screening result, **not a panel load rating**: it assumes a straight panel, centred loading and effective sideways restraint at both ends. It shows why sideways restraint and the load connection deserve attention, rather than automatically making the top band deeper. The material inputs and veneer-code interpretation come from [IBuilt’s product sheet](https://nzwoodproducts.co.nz/media/products/files/2024/PJC0434-NZWood-IBuild_Structural_Plywood-Product_information_sheet-BPIR-v1.pdf) and [structural guide](https://nzwoodproducts.co.nz/media/products/files/2023/PJC0331-NZWood-IBuilt_Structural_Plywood_Guide-A4-v5_2GpnUaE.pdf); the calculation follows the plywood section-property approach in the [EWPAA guide](https://www.plywoodandpanel.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/EWPAA-Structural-Plywood-LVL-Design-Guide-v5-FINAL-1.pdf).

**Here is the practical detail I would develop:**

| Parameter | Starting value |
|---|---:|
| Solid panel | **7 mm** |
| Bonded reinforcement | **7 mm** |
| Top-band depth | **50 mm** |
| End-strip width | **50 mm** |
| Maximum local thickness | **14 mm** |
| Internal corners | Rounded |

The 50 mm strips provide room for bonding and connections and reinforce the edges. **The calculation does not establish that 50 mm is the minimum**; it supports testing this modest detail rather than the earlier oversized one.

For the cross-bench panel, the material comparison is:

| Reinforcement width/depth | Material volume relative to a solid 16 mm panel* |
|---|---:|
| 40 mm U | **52%** |
| 50 mm U | **54%** |
| 60 mm U | **55%** |

*Same panel dimensions; equal density for the weight comparison; excludes adhesive and fittings.*

There are two specific limits to carry into the design:

- **A floor gap, door opening or unsupported bottom changes the calculation.** The continuous sheet is doing useful work.
- **The grain orientation matters.** This numerical check cannot automatically be transferred to a long panel cut in the other direction.

With continuous floor support, a middle reinforcement on the long bench is therefore **not automatically required just because it is longer**. Its purpose would be to improve sideways stability or support a connection. That gives us a much lighter basis to develop than treating every panel as an open frame.

**Use a 25 mm inside radius as our baseline** where the 50 mm top band meets each upright.

That’s a practical design choice, **not a calculated minimum**. Rounded internal corners avoid the sharp notches that concentrate stress; the general principle is supported by [WEST SYSTEM’s Epoxyworks guidance](https://www.epoxyworks.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/23-Epoxyworks.pdf).

Keep the straight bands **50 mm wide**, with the curve **leaving extra material in the corner**, rather than cutting into those bands. It adds negligible material and no extra thickness into storage.

For fabrication, a **50 mm-diameter drilled hole** can form each R25 corner, with the straight cuts meeting it tangentially. In the model, we’ll use a named **`insideCornerRadius = 25 mm`** parameter.

> sounds great. can we parameterise the 50mm as  well?

Yes. We’ll use:

- **`reinforcementWidth = 50 mm`** — controls both the top-band depth and upright widths.
- **`insideCornerRadius = 25 mm`** — controls the inside curves independently.
- **`plyThickness = 7 mm`** — controls both layers.

Changing `reinforcementWidth` will regenerate the entire U shape consistently. These are the agreed parameters; I haven’t added them to Onshape yet.

> FeatureScript 3095 modelling notes (2026-10-14):
> - In test_featurescript, the second lambda argument is a queries map, even though the tool examples call it id. For geometry operations inside the evaluation lambda, create an Id explicitly with makeId("probe"). Adding a string to the second argument fails with 'Can not add map and string'.
> - 'box' is reserved syntax; do not name a helper function box. Renaming it makeBlock fixed a 'no features found' compilation failure.
> - A zero-thickness footprint can be made with newSketchOnPlane, skPolyline, skSolve, then opExtractSurface with faces:qSketchRegion(sketchId) and offset:0*centimeter. qCreatedBy(surfaceId,EntityType.BODY) resolves the resulting surface.
> - qBodyType(...,BodyType.SHEET) includes sketch region bodies. Use qSketchFilter(query,SketchObject.NO) when counting actual surface parts.
> - test_feature invokes the first exported feature. Place a self-contained validation feature before the production feature when testing both together. Exact geometry bounds and volumes can be checked with evBox3d(...tight:true) and evVolume; assert failures surface as notices, sometimes INFO, so inspect messages rather than relying on isError alone.
> ```

L*H-2*(bay*(H-2*W)-(4-PI)*R^2);\n        const frameArea = L*H-2*(bay*(H-W)-(2-PI/2)*R^2);\n        check(abs((evVolume(context,{\"entities\":skin})-skinArea*d.wallThickness)/millimeter^3)<0.1,\"Skin opening volume\");\n        check(abs((evVolume(context,{\"entities\":frame})-frameArea*d.frameThickness)/millimeter^3)<0.1,\"Frame arch volume\");\n        const bounds = evBox3d(context,{\"topology\":frame,\"tight\":true});\n        check(norm((bounds.minCorner-vector(d.seatWidth-d.wallThickness-d.frameThickness,0*millimeter,0*millimeter))/millimeter)<0.001,\"Frame minimum\");\n        check(norm((bounds.maxCorner-vector(d.seatWidth-d.wallThickness,L,H))/millimeter)<0.001,\"Frame maximum\");\n        const cross = evBox3d(context,{\"topology\":qCreatedBy(caseId+\"crossBench\",EntityType.BODY),\"tight\":true});\n        check(norm((cross.maxCorner-vector(d.bedWidth-d.crossExtension,d.cargoLength,H))/millimeter)<0.001,\"Cross bench dimensions\");\n        check(abs((getVariable(context,\"nv200_longHatchWidth\")-bay)/millimeter)<0.001,\"Hatch variable\");\n        results = append(results,{\"case\":c,\"parts\":size(evaluateQuery(context,solids)),\n            \"hatchWidthMm\":bay/millimeter,\"hatchHeightMm\":(H-2*W)/millimeter});\n        opDeleteBodies(context,makeId(\"cleanup\" ~ c),{\"entities\":qCreatedBy(caseId,EntityType.BODY)});\n    }\n    return results;\n\n}"

> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });

>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),

>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });

> }

**The first construction pass is saved in Onshape.** The solid bench boxes are replaced with separate plywood walls and frames.

- **7 mm outer walls; 18 mm inner frames; 60 mm bands/posts.**
- Long bench: two **550 × 262 mm** access openings, with rounded corners.
- Cross bench: **870 × 580 mm**, reserving the 200 mm extension.
- Platform height: **400 mm**, giving **382 mm panels** beneath the 18 mm slats.

These are editable parameters. Geometry and regeneration checks passed; saved source was verified, though I haven’t visually inspected the updated Part Studio.

**Next is the interlocking slat layout and its moving support frame.** Hatch doors and sliding parts aren’t modelled yet; cushions remain labelled layout references.

> remember that the side of the cross bench needs a gap to the floor, for the toilet

> /** Each wall is two distinct parts: an outer skin and a cut-out inner plywood frame. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             ["memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1 || access)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // Toilet-side opening reaches the floor through both layers; hatch skins retain their lower band.
>                 const bottom = layer == 0 && !floorAccess ? w : -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {

>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }

> /** Opposite long walls run full length; the end walls fit between the combined wall/frame thicknesses. */
> function benchCarcass(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, y, width, length,
>     height, longBays is number, rightAccess is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)

>     benchWall(context, id+"right", name ~ " aisle side", vector(x+width,y+length,zero),
>         vector(0,-1,0), vector(-1,0,0), length,height,longBays,rightAccess,floorAccess,d);
>     benchWall(context, id+"rear", name ~ " rear end", vector(x+width-total,y,zero),
>         vector(-1,0,0), vector(0,1,0), width-2*total,height,1,false,false,d);
>     benchWall(context, id+"front", name ~ " cab end", vector(x+total,y+length,zero),
>         vector(1,0,0), vector(0,-1,0), width-2*total,height,1,false,false,d);
> }

**I found reliable width information and a useful height measurement, but not a confirmed arch length or distance from the rear doors for the standard 4.4 m NV200.**

| Dimension | Finding | Confidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Clear width between wheel arches | **1,220 mm** | Nissan specification |
| Maximum cargo width | **1,500 mm** | Nissan specification |
| Arch height above a fitted floor | **Approximately 250 mm** | Owner-measured; varies with floor thickness |
| Arch length, front to back | **Unconfirmed** | No suitable dimensioned source found |
| Arch position relative to rear threshold | **Unconfirmed** | Needs measurement to place accurately |

The width figures come from [Nissan’s NV200 brochure, page 9](https://www.nissan-cdn.net/content/dam/Nissan/za/brochures/PANEL_VAN.pdf). The height comes from a [measured 2015 UK NV200 conversion](https://thetinycampervan.com/2020/05/11/dimensions-for-converting-an-nv200/); the author explicitly corrects the photograph’s height label to approximately 250 mm.

For our **simplified 1,500 mm-wide model**, assuming symmetry, the 1,220 mm gap would put the inner arch faces at **X=140 and X=1,360 mm**. That is a derived modelling position—not a measurement of each arch’s projection from the actual curved wall.

**The design implication:** the arches should sit below our 400 mm platform, but the wall-side plywood panels and posts need to accommodate them. We cannot yet position those cut-outs accurately along the van.

Two misleading sources came up: the longer North American NV200’s body-builder drawings, and a TRIMAT drawing for an insulated conversion. I haven’t transferred their dimensions into your model.

The remaining measurements needed are **rear threshold to the rear edge of each arch, arch length, and height above your floor**. Those will let us place the obstructions and adjust the affected panels without changing our agreed construction.

> can you deduce rough arch length and position from this drawing?
>
> User context
>
> Images:
> - `/var/folders/h4/392kvc197lq5sryyhh9jpfb40000gn/T/codex-clipboard-861fe472-c3b0-40f0-b456-7113b49eac7e.png`

**Yes—roughly 800 mm long, centred about 800 mm forward of the rear bumper.**

Scaling the side view against its labelled **4,560 mm overall length** gives:

| Feature | Approximate distance forward from rear bumper |
|---|---:|
| Rear edge of visible wheel opening | **400 mm** |
| Rear wheel centre | **800 mm** |
| Front edge of visible wheel opening | **1,200 mm** |
| Opening length | **800 mm** |

Treat these as estimates to roughly **±50–100 mm**, rather than precise dimensions.

Two distinctions matter when putting this into our model:

- This shows the **exterior wheel opening**. The interior wheel housing may extend beyond it.
- Our **Y=0 is the rear cargo-floor edge**, whereas these measurements start at the bumper. Subtract the bumper-to-floor-edge distance from both position values.

That places the arches approximately alongside the **rear-to-middle portion of the long bench**, where its wall-side centre post could interfere. It gives us a useful provisional location for designing the cut-out, with the final housing outline still to be measured.

Using its **2,725 mm wheelbase** as the scale:

That agrees reasonably with the previous estimate. This drawing also shows the **4,400 mm NV200**, making it the more relevant reference than the e-NV200 drawing.

For a provisional model, **800 mm long and centred 840 mm from the rear bumper** is a sensible starting point. We still need to account for the rear floor’s offset from the bumper, and the interior housing extending beyond the exterior opening. The top view doesn’t show the housings clearly enough to refine those.

> does this interfere with the vertical mid support on the "wall side" of the long bench?

**Yes—very likely.** The wall-side centre post is at **Y=640 mm**, halfway along the 1,280 mm bench. That falls within the estimated wheel-arch length, even allowing for the bumper-to-floor offset.

Because that post currently reaches the floor against the wall, it would run through the wheel housing.

The **aisle-side centre post can stay**. On the wall side, we should position posts **just ahead of and behind the arch**, with the top band continuing above it. This keeps our **18 mm plywood frame and 60 mm bands/posts**; only the post positions and wall cut-out change.

The new wall-side frame will retain its end posts and top band, with **two 60 mm posts flanking a 900 mm clear opening**: the estimated 800 mm arch plus 50 mm each side. The 7 mm wall panel will go.

One position is still missing: our arch estimate starts at the **bumper**, but the model starts at the **rear floor edge**.

For example, a **200 mm bumper-to-floor setback** would give:

| Item | Y position from rear floor edge |
|---|---:|
| Rear intermediate post | 130–190 mm |
| Estimated wheel arch | 240–1,040 mm |
| Front intermediate post | 1,090–1,150 mm |

**Shall we use that 200 mm setback as an explicitly provisional parameter?** It fits the requested arrangement within the 1,280 mm bench. I haven’t saved this change yet because that setback hasn’t been established.

That suggests an interior housing running approximately **Y=216–965 mm from the rear floor edge** in the illustrated van. It broadly supports our earlier **750–800 mm length estimate**.

**However, this drawing explicitly says 115″ wheelbase—approximately 2,921 mm.** Your previous drawing shows **2,725 mm**, so this is the longer variant. These are useful provisional dimensions, not confirmed measurements of your van.

Also, the **216 mm is rear floor space before the arch**, not the bumper-to-floor setback I previously asked about. With a drawing like this, we can locate the arch directly from the floor and avoid that extra calculation.

> // Preserve a filled rectangular bed and the continuous left-wall backrest.
> // These dependencies are intentional, not independent measurements.
> function layoutDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {
>     const p = {
>         "baseHeight" : d.platformHeight,
>         "infillWidth" : (d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth) / 2,
>         "dLength" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c2Length" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c1Length" : 2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength,
>         "cabinetDepth" : d.cargoWidth - d.bedWidth,
>         "aisleWidth" : d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth,
>         "innerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetInnerLength,
>         "outerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetOuterLength,
>         "frontUnbacked" : d.bedWidth - d.foamThickness - (2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength)
>     };
>     if (p.baseHeight <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Platform height must be positive.", ["platformHeight"]);
>     if (d.bedWidth <= d.seatWidth || d.cargoWidth <= d.bedWidth)
>         throw regenError("Require cargo width > bed width > long bench width.",
>             ["cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "seatWidth"]);
>     if (d.foamThickness >= d.seatWidth || d.foamThickness >= p.dLength)
>         throw regenError("Upright foam must fit on both seat cushions.", ["foamThickness"]);
>     if (p.c1Length <= 0 * centimeter || p.c2Length <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Long bench length must exceed half the cargo length and remain shorter than it.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength"]);
>     if (p.frontUnbacked < 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("The reference cab-facing cushion is too long for this bed width and foam thickness.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength", "bedWidth", "foamThickness"]);
>     if (d.cabinetInnerLength > d.cabinetOuterLength || p.outerGap < 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Require cabinet inner length <= outer length <= long bench length.",
>             ["cabinetInnerLength", "cabinetOuterLength", "seatLength"]);
>     return p;
> }

> function makeBlock(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, lo is Vector, hi is Vector, appearance is Color)
> {
>     fCuboid(context, id, { "corner1" : lo, "corner2" : hi });
>     nameAndColor(context, qCreatedBy(id, EntityType.BODY), name, appearance);
> }

> function footprintSketch(context is Context, id is Id, points is array)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id, {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * centimeter, vector(0, 0, 1), vector(1, 0, 0))
>     });
>     skPolyline(sketch, "outline", { "points" : points });
>     skSolve(sketch);
> }

> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }
>
> /** Each wall is two distinct parts: an outer skin and a cut-out inner plywood frame. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             ["memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1 || access)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // Toilet-side opening reaches the floor through both layers; hatch skins retain their lower band.
>                 const bottom = layer == 0 && !floorAccess ? w : -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }
>
>
> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, x, y, length, height, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const rearSupportEnd = d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance;
>     const postStart = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+w;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || postEnd > length-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.",
>             ["archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "memberWidth", "seatLength"]);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.",
>             ["archHeight", "platformHeight", "slatThickness", "memberWidth"]);
>     const origin = vector(x+d.wallThickness,y,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.",
>                     ["insideRadius", "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "seatLength"]);
>             if (i == 0 && d.archClearance < radius)
>             {
>                 const cornerHeight = height-w-radius+
>                     sqrt(radius^2-(radius-d.archClearance)^2);
>                 if (d.archHeight > cornerHeight)
>                     throw regenError("Wheel arch intersects the rounded opening corners.",
>                         ["archHeight", "archClearance", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>             }
>             const cutId = id+("opening" ~ i);
>             openingTool(context,cutId,origin-vector(1,0,0)*millimeter,
>                 vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),bounds[0],bounds[1],-2*radius,height-w,
>                 radius,d.frameThickness+2*millimeter);
>             opBoolean(context,cutId+"subtract",{
>                 "tools":qCreatedBy(cutId+"solid",EntityType.BODY),
>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }
>     nameAndColor(context,frame,"Long bench wall-side frame - wheel-arch opening",color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);
> }

**750 mm is plausible, but I haven’t confirmed it for your van.** Your drawing labels the housing length as 29½″, which converts to 749 mm.

Two things make our model look oversized:

- I represented it as a **full rectangular block**. The real housing has rounded ends and shoulders, so occupies less space.
- The drawing is labelled **115″ wheelbase**—the longer North American variant. Its measurements aren’t definitive for yours.

Keep 750 mm as a provisional clearance envelope until tomorrow’s measurement. I shouldn’t have presented that block as though it accurately represented your wheel arch.

> Here's a photo showing the 122cm width between arches. it's roughly 25cm high. deduce what the length would be at its base
>
> User context
>
> Images:
> - `/var/folders/h4/392kvc197lq5sryyhh9jpfb40000gn/T/codex-clipboard-efd8c5e7-4024-48ca-8f2f-36bf23222671.png`

**This photo doesn’t give a reliable base length.** The 122 cm width runs across the image, while the arch’s length runs away from the camera and is foreshortened. The 25 cm height doesn’t resolve that perspective.

So **750 mm remains plausible, but this photo doesn’t verify it**. Giving you a narrower estimate would imply more accuracy than the evidence supports.

What it does show clearly is that my rectangular block exaggerates the occupied space: the real housing has strongly rounded shoulders and sloping ends. A side-on photograph with the known 25 cm height would let us estimate its base length much more reliably.

> function layoutDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {
>     const p = {
>         "baseHeight" : d.platformHeight,
>         "infillWidth" : (d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth) / 2,
>         "dLength" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c2Length" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c1Length" : 2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength,
>         "cabinetDepth" : d.cargoWidth - d.bedWidth,
>         "aisleWidth" : d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth,
>         "innerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetInnerLength,
>         "outerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetOuterLength,
>         "frontUnbacked" : d.bedWidth - d.foamThickness - (2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength)
>     };
>     if (p.baseHeight <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Platform height must be positive.", ["platformHeight"]);
>     if (d.bedWidth <= d.seatWidth || d.cargoWidth <= d.bedWidth)
>         throw regenError("Require cargo width > bed width > long bench width.",
>             ["cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "seatWidth"]);
>     if (d.foamThickness >= d.seatWidth || d.foamThickness >= p.dLength)
>         throw regenError("Upright foam must fit on both seat cushions.", ["foamThickness"]);
>     if (p.c1Length <= 0 * centimeter || p.c2Length <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Long bench length must exceed half the cargo length and remain shorter than it.",

> }

> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }
>
> /** Each wall is two distinct parts: an outer skin and a cut-out inner plywood frame. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             ["memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1 || access)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // Toilet-side opening reaches the floor through both layers; hatch skins retain their lower band.
>                 const bottom = layer == 0 && !floorAccess ? w : -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }
>
>
>
> /** Rounded upper ends only: editable visual approximation, with the full base footprint retained. */
> function wheelArchReference(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, depth, d is map)
> {
>     const r = d.archRadius;
>     const length = d.archLength;
>     const height = d.archHeight;
>     if (r <= 0*millimeter || 2*r >= length || r >= height)
>         throw regenError("Arch rounding radius must be positive, below its height and below half its length.",
>             ["archRadius", "archLength", "archHeight"]);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const k = 1-1/sqrt(2);
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id+"profile",{
>         "sketchPlane":plane(vector(x,d.archRearOffset,zero),vector(1,0,0),vector(0,1,0))
>     });
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"base",{"start":vector(zero,zero),"end":vector(length,zero)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"front",{"start":vector(length,zero),"end":vector(length,height-r)});
>     skArc(sketch,"frontRound",{"start":vector(length,height-r),
>         "mid":vector(length-k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(length-r,height)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"top",{"start":vector(length-r,height),"end":vector(r,height)});
>     skArc(sketch,"rearRound",{"start":vector(r,height),
>         "mid":vector(k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(zero,height-r)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"rear",{"start":vector(zero,height-r),"end":vector(zero,zero)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"body",{"entities":qSketchRegion(id+"profile"),"direction":vector(1,0,0),
>         "endBound":BoundingType.BLIND,"endDepth":depth});
>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"body",EntityType.BODY),name,color(0.45,0.49,0.52));
> }
>
> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, x, y, length, height, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const rearSupportEnd = d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance;
>     const postStart = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+w;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || postEnd > length-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.",
>             ["archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "memberWidth", "seatLength"]);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.",
>             ["archHeight", "platformHeight", "slatThickness", "memberWidth"]);
>     const origin = vector(x+d.wallThickness,y,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.",
>                     ["insideRadius", "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "seatLength"]);
>             if (i == 0 && d.archClearance < radius)
>             {
>                 const cornerHeight = height-w-radius+
>                     sqrt(radius^2-(radius-d.archClearance)^2);
>                 if (d.archHeight > cornerHeight)
>                     throw regenError("Wheel arch intersects the rounded opening corners.",
>                         ["archHeight", "archClearance", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>             }
>             const cutId = id+("opening" ~ i);
>             openingTool(context,cutId,origin-vector(1,0,0)*millimeter,
>                 vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),bounds[0],bounds[1],-2*radius,height-w,
>                 radius,d.frameThickness+2*millimeter);
>             opBoolean(context,cutId+"subtract",{
>                 "tools":qCreatedBy(cutId+"solid",EntityType.BODY),
>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }
>     nameAndColor(context,frame,"Long bench wall-side frame - wheel-arch opening",color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);
> }
>
> /** Opposite long walls run full length; the end walls fit between the combined wall/frame thicknesses. */
> function benchCarcass(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, y, width, length,
>     height, longBays is number, rightAccess is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, archSide is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const total = d.wallThickness+d.frameThickness;
>     if (width <= 2*total || length <= 2*total)
>         throw regenError("Bench width and depth must exceed twice the combined wall and frame thickness.",
>             ["wallThickness", "frameThickness", "seatWidth", "seatLength", "cargoLength", "crossExtension"]);
>     if (archSide)
>         wheelArchFrame(context,id+"left",x,y,length,height,d);
>     else
>         benchWall(context, id+"left", name ~ " wall side", vector(x,y,zero),
>             vector(0,1,0), vector(1,0,0), length,height,longBays,false,false,d);
>     benchWall(context, id+"right", name ~ " aisle side", vector(x+width,y+length,zero),
>         vector(0,-1,0), vector(-1,0,0), length,height,longBays,rightAccess,floorAccess,d);
>     benchWall(context, id+"rear", name ~ " rear end", vector(x+width-total,y,zero),
>         vector(-1,0,0), vector(0,1,0), width-2*total,height,1,false,false,d);
>     benchWall(context, id+"front", name ~ " cab end", vector(x+total,y+length,zero),
>         vector(1,0,0), vector(0,-1,0), width-2*total,height,1,false,false,d);
> }
>

> function layoutDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {

>         "infillWidth" : (d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth) / 2,
>         "dLength" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c2Length" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,

> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }

> /** Each wall is two distinct parts: an outer skin and a cut-out inner plywood frame. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             ["memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1 || access)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // Toilet-side opening reaches the floor through both layers; hatch skins retain their lower band.
>                 const bottom = layer == 0 && !floorAccess ? w : -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }

> /** Rounded upper ends only: editable visual approximation, with the full base footprint retained. */

> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, x, y, length, height, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const rearSupportEnd = d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance;
>     const postStart = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+w;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || postEnd > length-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.",
>             ["archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "memberWidth", "seatLength"]);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.",
>             ["archHeight", "platformHeight", "slatThickness", "memberWidth"]);
>     const origin = vector(x+d.wallThickness,y,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.",
>                     ["insideRadius", "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "seatLength"]);
>             if (i == 0 && d.archClearance < radius)

>                 const cornerHeight = height-w-radius+

>                 if (d.archHeight > cornerHeight)
>                     throw regenError("Wheel arch intersects the rounded opening corners.",
>                         ["archHeight", "archClearance", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>             }
>             const cutId = id+("opening" ~ i);
>             openingTool(context,cutId,origin-vector(1,0,0)*millimeter,
>                 vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),bounds[0],bounds[1],-2*radius,height-w,
>                 radius,d.frameThickness+2*millimeter);
>             opBoolean(context,cutId+"subtract",{
>                 "tools":qCreatedBy(cutId+"solid",EntityType.BODY),
>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }
>     nameAndColor(context,frame,"Long bench wall-side frame - wheel-arch opening",color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);
> }

> // Preserve a filled rectangular bed and the continuous left-wall backrest.
> // These dependencies are intentional, not independent measurements.
> function layoutDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {
>     const p = {
>         "baseHeight" : d.platformHeight,
>         "infillWidth" : (d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth) / 2,
>         "dLength" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c2Length" : d.cargoLength - d.seatLength,
>         "c1Length" : 2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength,
>         "cabinetDepth" : d.cargoWidth - d.bedWidth,
>         "aisleWidth" : d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth,
>         "innerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetInnerLength,
>         "outerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetOuterLength,
>         "frontUnbacked" : d.bedWidth - d.foamThickness - (2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength)
>     };
>     if (p.baseHeight <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Platform height must be positive.", ["platformHeight"]);
>     if (d.bedWidth <= d.seatWidth || d.cargoWidth <= d.bedWidth)
>         throw regenError("Require cargo width > bed width > long bench width.",
>             ["cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "seatWidth"]);
>     if (d.foamThickness >= d.seatWidth || d.foamThickness >= p.dLength)
>         throw regenError("Upright foam must fit on both seat cushions.", ["foamThickness"]);
>     if (p.c1Length <= 0 * centimeter || p.c2Length <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Long bench length must exceed half the cargo length and remain shorter than it.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength"]);
>     if (p.frontUnbacked < 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("The reference cab-facing cushion is too long for this bed width and foam thickness.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength", "bedWidth", "foamThickness"]);
>     if (d.cabinetInnerLength > d.cabinetOuterLength || p.outerGap < 0 * centimeter)

>             ["cabinetInnerLength", "cabinetOuterLength", "seatLength"]);

> function footprintSketch(context is Context, id is Id, points is array)
> {

>     skSolve(sketch);

> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }

> /** Each wall is two distinct parts: an outer skin and a cut-out inner plywood frame. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, floorAccess is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             ["memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight"]);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1 || access)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // Toilet-side opening reaches the floor through both layers; hatch skins retain their lower band.
>                 const bottom = layer == 0 && !floorAccess ? w : -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }

> /** Door reference outlines only; rectangles do not imply body contours, door leaves or travel paths. */
> function doorOutline(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, along is Vector, width, height)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id,{"sketchPlane":plane(origin,normal,along)});

>     for (var i = 0; i < 4; i += 1)
>         skLineSegment(sketch,"edge" ~ i,{"start":corners[i],"end":corners[(i+1)%4],"construction":true});

>     setProperty(context,{"entities":qCreatedBy(id,EntityType.BODY),"propertyType":PropertyType.NAME,"value":name});

> /** Rounded upper ends only: editable visual approximation, with the full base footprint retained. */
> function wheelArchReference(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, depth, d is map)
> {

>     const length = d.archLength;
>     const height = d.archHeight;

>     skArc(sketch,"frontRound",{"start":vector(length,height-r),
>         "mid":vector(length-k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(length-r,height)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"top",{"start":vector(length-r,height),"end":vector(r,height)});
>     skArc(sketch,"rearRound",{"start":vector(r,height),
>         "mid":vector(k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(zero,height-r)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"rear",{"start":vector(zero,height-r),"end":vector(zero,zero)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"body",{"entities":qSketchRegion(id+"profile"),"direction":vector(1,0,0),

>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"body",EntityType.BODY),name,color(0.45,0.49,0.52));

> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, x, y, length, height, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const rearSupportEnd = d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance;
>     const postStart = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+w;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || postEnd > length-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.",
>             ["archRearOffset", "archLength", "archClearance", "memberWidth", "seatLength"]);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.",
>             ["archHeight", "platformHeight", "slatThickness", "memberWidth"]);
>     const origin = vector(x+d.wallThickness,y,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.",

>             if (i == 0 && d.archClearance < radius)

>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }

>     setVariable(context,"nv200_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);

> nice. Ok a couple of things: the rear door dimensions look alright, but it's important to note that there is an *inside corner* of about 10cm radius (concave) in the rear corners, forming the post and blending the rear with the side. we need that, and we need to change the shape of our bench in that corner to allow for that + tolerances. Suggest something that is still relatively easy to build. NOTE that it is extremely unlikely that that corner will have any load, so we could shorten both frames by 12cm there, and we'll deal with a shortened slat later. In my existing bed, the rear-most slat is 1200mm (while the rest is 1400mm)

> A straight diagonal cut across a 120 × 120 mm corner looks like the simplest option: it clears the approximate 100 mm body radius without needing curved plywood parts. I’ll check how that affects the rear support we just widened.
