**For your layout, I’d use it primarily for outdoor gear, spare clothing and daytime bedding storage.** Anything needed after extending the bed should have another home.

The examples I found follow that pattern:

- **Chairs, folding tables and levelling ramps:** owners describe keeping these under the bed for use outside. [Owner discussion](https://www.reddit.com/r/VanLife/comments/12q5eab/pull_out_storage_plan_for_van/)
- **Outdoor equipment, backpacks, tools and seasonal gear:** FarOutRide uses its under-bed garage for these, deliberately putting off-season equipment in harder-to-access spaces. [Their actual storage layout](https://faroutride.com/garage/)
- **Bedding bags, camping chairs and awning equipment:** these are stated uses for SpaceMate’s rear pull-out trays. That is a manufacturer’s suggested packing list, rather than an owner survey. [SpaceMate](https://www.spacematedirect.com/en/vw-california-ocean-rear-storage)

For **our drawer**, I would prioritise:

| Contents | How it works with no inside access at night |
|---|---|
| Compact chairs, small folding table, picnic mat | Used outside; rear access suits them |
| Walking/day-trip equipment | Usually retrieved before leaving the van |
| Spare clothes in packing cubes | Keep tonight’s and tomorrow morning’s clothes elsewhere |
| Duvet/sleeping bags and pillows during the day | Remove them **before** extending the bed; they’re already out when access disappears |
| Small repair kit, spare equipment | Occasional access, usually from outside |

Bedding is particularly compatible with the conversion routine, **provided its packed volume fits**. It also gives a useful purpose to the drawer without making it carry lots of heavy equipment.

I would keep **toiletries, medication, torch, chargers, drinking water, an extra warm layer and breakfast essentials** accessible from bed. Everyday cooking equipment also deserves accessible cabinet space if you want to make breakfast before retracting the bed.

**My starting allocation would be bedding and spare clothes in removable soft bags, plus a separate section for compact outdoor gear.** Avoid permanent dividers until we know the packed sizes—especially the chairs and bedding. That gives us a concrete storage purpose while keeping the drawer light and adaptable.

**Yes. We can design around standard containers, and we may not need to widen the bench.** A useful first candidate is the **Sistema 27 L**, which is only **322 mm wide**.

Dimensions below are external, with the longest dimension running along the drawer:

| Container | Length × width × height | Implication |
|---|---:|---|
| [Sistema 27 L](https://www.sistemaplastics.com/nz/27l) | **494 × 322 × 258 mm** | Promising at our existing bench width. Two occupy 988 mm along the drawer. |
| [Euro-format crate, approximately 20 L](https://sarstorageprd.blob.core.windows.net/website-pim-media/103571.pdf) | **397 × 297 × 235 mm** | Narrower, modular option. Three occupy 1191 mm **before clearance**, so a nominal 1200 mm drawer would be tight. |
| [Euro-format crate, approximately 44 L](https://sarstorageprd.blob.core.windows.net/website-pim-media/103571.pdf) | **597 × 397 × 235 mm** | More generous for wet gear, but likely requires a wider bench with conventional side-mounted runners. |
| [Sistema 40 L](https://www.sistemaplastics.com/nz/40l) | **494 × 322 × 387 mm** | Too tall beneath our 400 mm platform once slats and drawer construction are included. |

Our current **412 mm space beside the wheel arch is not the drawer’s internal width**: runners, their mounting supports, drawer sides and clearance all come out of it. A 322 mm container leaves **90 mm for that construction**; a 397 mm container leaves only **15 mm**.

The rear opening also still needs redesigning, as discussed—these are candidates for the proposed drawer, not confirmed fits in the unchanged model.

**For a wetsuit, I’d try the 27 L container first.** Whether it comfortably holds yours depends on its size, thickness and whether boots/gloves go in too. A solid, unperforated tub would contain drips; it would be temporary wet transport storage, with the suit removed to dry afterwards. [Rip Curl’s storage guidance](https://www.ripcurl.com/blogs/products/how-to-store-wetsuits) recommends drying it before longer-term storage.

If that feels cramped, a **roughly 600 × 400 mm crate** is a sensible larger target. A **650 mm fixed bench width** would be worth testing in CAD for that option, subject to runner selection:

| | Current | Wider proposal |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fixed bench width | 570 mm | 650 mm |
| Including retracted moving frame | 588 mm | 668 mm |
| Daytime aisle | 482 mm | 402 mm |

**I’d choose and test-pack the container before widening the bench.** The 27 L option could give you a dedicated wetsuit tub while preserving the existing aisle. Whole tubs would be removed through the rear; reaching their contents through the aisle openings is a separate clearance check.

**The most promising option is a pair of 1,200 mm, side-mounted, full-extension runners with a 53 mm-high profile.** That is a sensible starting point for our storage drawer; the larger 76 mm runners add bulk we haven’t established a need for.

I found these NZ listings. Prices are per pair, including GST, excluding delivery:

| Runner | Closed length | Profile: height × thickness | Published capacity | Price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [Instant Panel, non-locking](https://instantpanel.co.nz/product/drawer-slides-1200mm-x-53mm-heavy-duty-runners.html) | 1,200 mm | 53 × 19 mm | 61 kg | $179.99 |
| [Instant Panel, locking](https://instantpanel.co.nz/product/drawer-slides-1200mm-x-53mm-with-lock-heavy-duty-runners.html) | 1,200 mm | 53 × 19 mm | 61 kg | $194.99 |
| [Instant Panel, larger non-locking](https://instantpanel.co.nz/product/drawer-slides-1200mm-x-76mm-super-heavy-duty-runners.html) | 1,200 mm | 76 × 19.2 mm | 132 kg | $269.99 |

There is also a [Grabstore 1,200 mm locking pair for $64.09](https://grabstore.co.nz/products/ya-00-00-a1200mm-drawer-slides-runner), but it currently says **sold out**. It claims 125 kg with a similar 53 mm profile, without the length-specific load information provided by Instant Panel. I wouldn’t assume those ratings are directly comparable.

**What “100% extension” means**

A 1,200 mm runner provides roughly 1,200 mm of drawer travel: the telescoping assembly occupies approximately 2,400 mm when extended. The smaller Instant Panel models actually list 2,415 mm overall, implying 1,215 mm travel. That should expose a matching-length drawer, provided its mounting position isn’t substantially recessed behind the rear opening.

**How they mount**

These are three-piece telescoping ball-bearing slides:

- The **outer rail attaches to the stationary furniture**.
- The **inner rail attaches to the drawer side**.
- The middle rail extends between them.

For the 53 mm Instant Panel series, the installation guide specifies **19 ±0.5 mm clearance on each side**, with the runners vertical, level and parallel. The inner member disconnects using a release lever, so you can attach the two halves separately and then insert the drawer. It specifies M5 fixings. [Installation guide](https://instantpanel.co.nz/productfiles/drawer_slides/Drawer_slides_2053_Installation_Precautions_and_Instructions.pdf)

The locking version holds both fully closed and fully open. Its operating lever projects 45 mm, and the supplier asks for **50 mm clearance for it**. We need to accommodate that at the rear drawer front. [Locking runner details](https://instantpanel.co.nz/product/drawer-slides-1200mm-x-53mm-with-lock-heavy-duty-runners.html)

**What this means for our bench**

We need two straight mounting faces along the drawer. The aisle frame can provide attachment points, but **the wheel-arch side needs its own mounting support**. The runner cannot simply attach to the wheel arch.

This makes our earlier width estimate tighter than I suggested. Illustratively:

| Width allowance | mm |
|---|---:|
| Corridor beside the arch | 412 |
| One additional plywood mounting support | −18 |
| Two runners | −38 |
| Two proposed 7 mm drawer sides | −14 |
| **Remaining internal width** | **342** |

Your **330 mm crate leaves only 12 mm total** in that arrangement, before wheel-arch clearance or additional reinforcement. It remains plausible, but the mounting layout needs checking before we call it a confirmed fit.

We can use **local plywood reinforcement at the runner fixings** without making every drawer panel thick. Those supports must connect into the fixed structure, while keeping the aisle access openings useful.

My recommendation is to develop the mounting layout around the **53 mm locking pair**. Its 61 kg rating includes the drawer and contents and assumes an evenly distributed load; the supplier doesn’t publish a separate vehicle-use rating or runner weight. Those are the remaining product details to establish before purchase. **No reason yet to widen the bench or choose the larger runners.**

**The research supports 12 mm birch plywood as a credible starting point for the drawer—not the unsupported 7 mm sides I suggested.** I carried our furniture-skin thickness into a different structural job without justifying it.

These are actual builders’ specifications:

| Example | What they use | Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| [VanEquip NZ](https://vanequip.co.nz/pages/van-drawer-system) | **12 mm birch plywood drawers**, with 18 mm false floors/front surfaces | Commercial van storage. Normally uses plastic sliding strips, with metal runners offered as an alternative. |
| [The Ply Guys Sutherland](https://www.theplyguys.co.uk/post/our-sutherland-has-had-a-major-upgrade) | **12 mm birch plywood** for its large storage-drawer system | Commercial camper furniture for outdoor equipment and tools. Its advertised runner rating alone doesn’t establish the plywood’s capacity. |
| [FarOutRide slide-out storage trays](https://faroutride.com/slide-out-trays/) | **12 mm Baltic birch bottom and long sides**, 12 mm bamboo ends | Particularly relevant to our low-sided tray: glued finger joints connect the bottom and sides; screws hold the assembly while the glue cures. |

**The construction matters as much as the thickness.** FarOutRide’s example is a joined tray whose bottom and sides work together. It isn’t a loose sheet carried by two thin side panels. Their runners also have dedicated mounting brackets; the stationary attachment is a separate structural component.

For another concrete mounting example, [Greysand’s 1,200 mm vehicle drawers](https://greysand.com.au/how-to-build-truck-drawers/) use glued and mechanically fastened boxes, with screws followed by **6 mm bolts on the stationary runner attachments**. That supports treating the runner connections explicitly, rather than assuming a few short screws into our furniture skins will do.

For ours, my recommendation is:

- **Use 12 mm birch plywood as the drawer-box design baseline**, including the bottom. That has relevant precedents and avoids starting with an elaborate reinforcement scheme.
- Design the bottom-to-side joints and runner fixings together. Don’t assign the runner’s 61 kg rating to the finished drawer automatically.
- Keep the **aisle-access requirement** explicit. Large cutouts or very low sides change how the box resists bending and twisting; the commercial examples don’t validate any arbitrary cutout we make.
- Keep the agreed **7 mm skins and 18 mm furniture frames** as they are. This recommendation concerns the new moving drawer.

There is a real fit consequence. With the same provisional mounting arrangement:

**412 − 18 mm stationary support − 38 mm runners − 24 mm drawer sides = 332 mm internal width.**

That gives your 330 mm crate only **2 mm total clearance**, before arch clearance and projecting fixings. **That arrangement is too tight to adopt.** We need to revise the mounting arrangement or gain some width—not thin the drawer sides merely to make the arithmetic fit.

So: **12 mm birch is a researched baseline; the drawer’s joints, low-side geometry and mounting arrangement still need designing before we can call the assembly fit for purpose.**

The other cited examples explicitly use 12 mm birch. Both are relevant precedents, but I shouldn’t treat different plywood products and drawer constructions as interchangeable.

**With 20 kg of gear, we’d be around 31 kg total—about half the 61 kg capacity. With 30 kg of gear, around 41 kg—about two-thirds.** Those are load scenarios, not measured weights for your belongings.

For a tray approximately **1,200 × 360 mm**, made entirely from 12 mm birch:

| Item | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|
| Plywood bottom | 3.5 kg |
| Four sides, assuming 100–150 mm high | 2.5–3.8 kg |
| **Finished tray allowance**, including glue, finish and fixings | **8 kg** |
| Two empty plastic containers—provisional allowance | **3 kg** |
| **Tray and containers before packing** | **11 kg** |

The plywood calculation uses WISA’s published birch density of **680 kg/m³**, with some variation between sheets. Side height is an estimate here, not a settled design dimension. [WISA material data](https://www.wisaplywood.com/specifying-wisa/sizes-thicknesses-and-weights/)

That gives us:

| Contents: wetsuit, camping gear, etc. | Total including tray and tubs | Capacity used | Remaining |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 kg | 21 kg | 34% | 40 kg |
| 20 kg | 31 kg | 51% | 30 kg |
| 30 kg | 41 kg | 67% | 20 kg |
| 40 kg | 51 kg | 84% | 10 kg |

**So the 61 kg runners remain a reasonable candidate for this use.** We don’t currently have a weight-based reason to upgrade them. Water containers, tools and other dense items would consume the allowance much faster than clothing and bedding.

The supplier’s rating includes **drawer plus contents**, evenly distributed at full extension; it doesn’t establish the strength of our plywood joints or mounting supports. [Runner instructions](https://instantpanel.co.nz/productfiles/drawer_slides/Drawer_slides_2053_Installation_Precautions_and_Instructions.pdf)

The useful next check is simply to weigh your intended gear together—including the wetsuit wet—and replace the assumed contents weight with that number.

**For this drawer, steel tubing could provide strong joints and runner attachments, but I don’t see a clear weight or space advantage over 12 mm birch.** A lightweight steel version is possible; the complete frame and lining need comparing.

Using our approximate **1,200 × 360 mm tray with 150 mm-high sides**:

| Construction | Estimated material weight |
|---|---:|
| 12 mm birch bottom and four sides | **7.3 kg** |
| 20 × 20 × 1.6 mm steel bottom perimeter, plus two crossbars | **3.2 kg** |
| 6 mm birch bottom and four side covers for that steel frame | **3.6 kg** |
| **Steel frame plus plywood above** | **6.8 kg**, before any uprights, upper rails or mounting tabs |

These calculations use **0.87 kg/m for 20 × 20 × 1.6 mm steel tube** and **680 kg/m³ for birch plywood**. [Asmuss steel specifications](https://www.asmuss.co.nz/steel/products/steel/shs-rhs/square-hollow-section), [WISA plywood density](https://www.wisaplywood.com/specifying-wisa/sizes-thicknesses-and-weights/)

That steel arrangement is an illustrative weight estimate. Its joints, bottom support and runner attachment still require checking. **Its initial saving is only about half a kilogram**, which additional frame members could readily consume.

For your three criteria:

- **Stronger:** Steel offers useful resistance to local damage and can provide welded attachment points. Overall stiffness depends on the frame layout. The depth of a plywood drawer side contributes substantially to its stiffness, so replacing it with one small tube doesn’t automatically improve the assembly.
- **Lighter:** Potentially, with carefully selected thin-wall tubing and minimal lining. The ordinary 1.6 mm-wall sections above offer little apparent saving for this small tray.
- **Smaller:** At the side rails, **20 mm tubing occupies 8 mm more per side than 12 mm plywood**. Within the same outside width, that costs 16 mm of container space before adding any lining that projects beyond the tubing. Putting the frame beneath the tray instead consumes height.

Steel also adds cutting, welding or bracketed joints, and corrosion protection—particularly relevant around wet gear.

**I’d keep 12 mm birch as our drawer baseline.** Steel becomes more attractive if we need a very open frame or a particular mounting bracket. For the complete lined tray, the comparison so far gives us little reason to change materials.

> ok. how high are the slides?

The shortlisted slides are **53 mm high**, **19 mm thick per side**, and **1,200 mm long when closed**.

> could we construct something like we have for the frames, but inverted, and 12mm? Iike a "U" or "W" shape? With full height front and back panels?

**Yes—a 12 mm plywood tray with open, U-shaped longitudinal sides and full-height front and back panels is a sensible design to develop.** It would preserve access through the bench’s aisle openings.

Each long side would have:

- A **continuous bottom band** carrying the drawer slide.
- An upright at each end, joined to the full-height front and back panels.
- A large opening above the band.
- A **12 mm plywood bottom**, joined continuously to both side bands and the end panels.

The full-height ends connect the two sides and help keep the tray square. The bottom also ties the assembly together.

**I’d start with the U shape.** A W shape adds a middle upright, but a free-standing upright contributes little to supporting the drawer along its length. It becomes more useful when connected to a transverse divider or brace—which would need to suit the containers and aisle access.

Two details need resolving before we settle the dimensions:

1. **Bottom-band height:** the slides are 53 mm high, but we need their mounting-hole positions and sufficient plywood around the fixings. We shouldn’t automatically reuse the furniture’s 60 mm band.
2. **Strength of the open side:** removing the upper part changes the drawer’s stiffness. The bottom joint, band height and runner attachments need checking together against our intended load.

This is a promising way to save material and retain access. We can keep the front and back full height while putting the plywood where it supports the bottom and attaches to the runners.

> what would the bottom of the drawer be?

**One continuous sheet of 12 mm birch plywood**, joined along both long edges to the U-shaped sides and at each end to the front and back panels.

That sheet forms the tray floor, supports the containers and helps keep the drawer square. Its final width depends on the runner mounting arrangement.

> should the bottom be the full size with the sides resting on top? Or should the bottom fit "inside" the sides (like most furniture drawers?)

<details><summary>2 previous messages</summary>

> I’ll check the joint options for a low-sided tray on side-mounted runners, particularly how the bottom transfers its load into the sides.
>
> <details><summary>Searched the web</summary>
>
> Searched the web for `site.woodmagazine.com drawer bottom groove plywood bottom rabbet drawer construction ...`
>
> </details>
</details>

**I’d fit the bottom inside the sides, with its edges captured in glued grooves.**

Because the runners attach to the sides, the load travels from **contents → bottom → side panels → runners**. A groove provides a continuous plywood ledge beneath the bottom to carry that load. This is an established drawer construction method recommended by [WOOD Magazine](https://www.woodmagazine.com/woodworking-how-to/doors-drawers/drawers-101).

For our tray:

- Keep the **12 mm birch bottom**.
- Cut matching grooves into the inside faces of the sides, front and back.
- Glue the bottom into those grooves during assembly, helping keep the tray square.
- Position runner fixings in the full-thickness plywood above the groove.

A full-size bottom with the sides resting on it is simpler to assemble, but when the drawer hangs from its runners, the bottom’s attachment carries the contents through glue and fasteners. I prefer the continuous bearing provided by the grooved joint.

We should set the groove position alongside the runner holes so there is enough material beneath it and no fixing conflicts.

> eh ok how much material would sit *below* the groove? again you're just improvising instead of really thinking about this. any material below the groove means raising the bottom means less height in the drawer

You’re right. I hadn’t accounted for that height loss, and I hadn’t established a suitable thickness beneath the groove.

If we left **6 mm beneath a groove holding the 12 mm bottom**, the storage surface would sit **18 mm above the underside of the sides**. That costs 6 mm compared with a flush-bottom tray. **The 6 mm is an illustration, not a verified specification.**

I retract the groove recommendation for now. For our height constraint, we should develop a **flush-bottom joint**. FarOutRide’s glued finger-jointed tray is a relevant precedent already researched; it connects the bottom and sides without needing a ledge below the floor. Its fabrication requirements need considering before we adopt it.

I should have compared that construction and its height against the groove before recommending one.

> so bottom on the inside, glewed and screwed?

Yes—**bottom fitted between the sides, with its underside flush with their bottom edges, glued and screwed.** Screws go through the side panels into the edge of the 12 mm bottom, with pilot holes to reduce splitting.

That preserves the full usable height. Screw size, spacing and the glued joint still need specifying for our load; we haven’t verified those yet.

>         "aisleWidth" : d.bedWidth - d.seatWidth - d.frameThickness,
>         "innerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetOuterLength,
>         "outerGap" : d.seatLength - d.cabinetOuterLength,
>         "frontUnbacked" : d.bedWidth - d.foamThickness - (2 * d.seatLength - d.cargoLength)
>     };
>     if (p.baseHeight <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Platform height must be positive.", ["platformHeight"]);
>     if (d.bedWidth <= d.seatWidth || d.cargoWidth <= d.bedWidth)
>         throw regenError("Require cargo width > bed width > long bench width.",
>             ["cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "seatWidth"]);
>     if (d.foamThickness >= d.seatWidth || d.foamThickness >= p.dLength)
>         throw regenError("Upright foam must fit on both seat cushions.", ["foamThickness"]);
>     if (p.c1Length <= 0 * centimeter || p.c2Length <= 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Long bench length must exceed half the cargo length and remain shorter than it.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength"]);
>     if (p.frontUnbacked < 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("The reference cab-facing cushion is too long for this bed width and foam thickness.",
>             ["seatLength", "cargoLength", "bedWidth", "foamThickness"]);
>     if (p.outerGap < 0 * centimeter)
>         throw regenError("Cabinet length must not exceed the long bench length.",
>             ["cabinetOuterLength", "seatLength"]);
>     return p;
> }
>
>
> function nameAndColor(context is Context, bodies is Query, name is string, appearance is Color)
> {
>     setProperty(context, { "entities" : bodies, "propertyType" : PropertyType.NAME, "value" : name });
>     setProperty(context, { "entities" : bodies, "propertyType" : PropertyType.APPEARANCE, "value" : appearance });
> }
>
> function makeBlock(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, lo is Vector, hi is Vector, appearance is Color)
> {
>     fCuboid(context, id, { "corner1" : lo, "corner2" : hi });
>     nameAndColor(context, qCreatedBy(id, EntityType.BODY), name, appearance);
> }
>
> function footprintSketch(context is Context, id is Id, points is array)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id, {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * centimeter, vector(0, 0, 1), vector(1, 0, 0))
>     });
>     skPolyline(sketch, "outline", { "points" : points });
>     skSolve(sketch);
> }
>
> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }
>
> /** Access faces use an open-bottom frame only; closed faces also retain a solid outer skin. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, d is map, parameterIds is array)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             parameterIds);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = access ? 1 : 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 || access ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // All frame openings reach the floor; no cut-out outer skins are generated.
>                 const bottom = -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }
>
>
>
>
> /** Door reference outlines only; rectangles do not imply body contours, door leaves or travel paths. */
> function doorOutline(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, along is Vector, width, height)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id,{"sketchPlane":plane(origin,normal,along)});
>     const corners = [vector(zero,zero),vector(width,zero),vector(width,height),vector(zero,height)];
>     for (var i = 0; i < 4; i += 1)
>         skLineSegment(sketch,"edge" ~ i,{"start":corners[i],"end":corners[(i+1)%4],"construction":true});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     setProperty(context,{"entities":qCreatedBy(id,EntityType.BODY),"propertyType":PropertyType.NAME,"value":name});
> }
>
> /** Rounded upper ends only: editable visual approximation, with the full base footprint retained. */
> function wheelArchReference(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, depth, d is map)
> {
>     const r = d.archRadius;
>     const length = d.archLength;
>     const height = d.archHeight;
>     if (r <= 0*millimeter || 2*r >= length || r >= height)
>         throw regenError("Arch rounding radius must be positive, below its height and below half its length.",
>             ["archRadius", "archLength", "archHeight"]);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const k = 1-1/sqrt(2);
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id+"profile",{
>         "sketchPlane":plane(vector(x,d.archRearOffset,zero),vector(1,0,0),vector(0,1,0))
>     });
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"base",{"start":vector(zero,zero),"end":vector(length,zero)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"front",{"start":vector(length,zero),"end":vector(length,height-r)});
>     skArc(sketch,"frontRound",{"start":vector(length,height-r),
>         "mid":vector(length-k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(length-r,height)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"top",{"start":vector(length-r,height),"end":vector(r,height)});
>     skArc(sketch,"rearRound",{"start":vector(r,height),
>         "mid":vector(k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(zero,height-r)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"rear",{"start":vector(zero,height-r),"end":vector(zero,zero)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"body",{"entities":qSketchRegion(id+"profile"),"direction":vector(1,0,0),
>         "endBound":BoundingType.BLIND,"endDepth":depth});
>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"body",EntityType.BODY),name,color(0.45,0.49,0.52));
> }
>
>
> /** Concave rear body corner surface. Radius is provisional; height follows the rear opening reference. */
> function rearCornerReference(context is Context, id is Id, right is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const r = d.rearCornerRadius;
>     const k = 1-1/sqrt(2);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const x = right ? d.cargoWidth : zero;
>     const sign = right ? -1 : 1;
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id+"profile",{
>         "sketchPlane":plane(vector(zero,zero,zero),vector(0,0,1),vector(1,0,0))
>     });
>     skArc(sketch,"corner",{"start":vector(x+sign*r,zero),
>         "mid":vector(x+sign*k*r,k*r),"end":vector(x,r)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"surface",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.EDGE),
>         "direction":vector(0,0,1),"endBound":BoundingType.BLIND,
>         "endDepth":d.rearDoorSill+d.rearDoorHeight});
>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"surface",EntityType.BODY),
>         (right ? "Right" : "Left") ~ " rear body corner - approximate surface",color(0.55,0.58,0.61));
> }
>
> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, variablePrefix is string,
>     frameX, y, length, height, combineFrontPosts is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const parameterIds = variablePrefix == "nv200_cabinet" ?
>         ["cabinetHeight", "cabinetOuterLength", "memberWidth", "insideRadius",
>          "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archHeight", "archClearance", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"] :
>         ["platformHeight", "slatThickness", "seatLength", "memberWidth", "insideRadius",
>          "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archHeight", "archClearance", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"];
>     const setback = d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance;
>     const rearSupportEnd = max(d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance,setback+w);
>     const rearClearance = d.archRearOffset-rearSupportEnd;
>     if (rearClearance <= 0*millimeter)
>         throw regenError("Rear corner setback and post reach the wheel arch. Check measured dimensions.", parameterIds);
>     const archFront = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength;
>     // Adjacent uprights retain both member widths: 60 + 60 = 120 mm at baseline.
>     const postWidth = combineFrontPosts ? 2*w : w;
>     const postStart = combineFrontPosts ? length-postWidth : archFront+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+postWidth;
>     const frontClearance = postStart-archFront;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || frontClearance < d.archClearance ||
>         (!combineFrontPosts && postEnd > length-w))
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.", parameterIds);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.", parameterIds);
>     const origin = vector(frameX,y+setback,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length-setback,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = combineFrontPosts ? [[rearSupportEnd,postStart]] : [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.", parameterIds);
>             const endClearance = min(rearClearance,frontClearance);
>             if (i == 0 && endClearance < radius)
>             {
>                 const cornerHeight = height-w-radius+
>                     sqrt(radius^2-(radius-endClearance)^2);
>                 if (d.archHeight > cornerHeight)
>                     throw regenError("Wheel arch intersects the rounded opening corners.", parameterIds);
>             }
>             const cutId = id+("opening" ~ i);
>             openingTool(context,cutId,origin-vector(1,0,0)*millimeter,
>                 vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),bounds[0]-setback,bounds[1]-setback,-2*radius,height-w,
>                 radius,d.frameThickness+2*millimeter);
>             opBoolean(context,cutId+"subtract",{
>                 "tools":qCreatedBy(cutId+"solid",EntityType.BODY),
>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }
>     nameAndColor(context,frame,name ~ " wall-side frame - wheel-arch opening",color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd-setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportStart",y+setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportEnd",y+rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearArchClearance",rearClearance);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_frontArchClearance",frontClearance);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearCornerSetback",setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);
> }
>
> /** End walls fit the actual side build-ups: exposed frames sit at the nominal aisle boundary. */
> function benchCarcass(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, y, width, length,
>     height, longBays is number, rightAccess is boolean, archSide is string, d is map)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const parameterIds = archSide == "RIGHT" ?
>         ["wallThickness", "frameThickness", "memberWidth", "insideRadius", "cabinetHeight",
>          "cabinetOuterLength", "cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"] :
>         ["wallThickness", "frameThickness", "memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight",
>          "slatThickness", "seatWidth", "seatLength", "cargoLength", "crossExtension"];
>     const total = d.wallThickness+d.frameThickness;
>     const leftInset = archSide == "RIGHT" && rightAccess ? d.frameThickness : total;
>     const rightInset = archSide != "RIGHT" && rightAccess ? d.frameThickness : total;
>     if (width <= leftInset+rightInset || length <= 2*total)
>         throw regenError("Carcass width and length must leave room between opposing walls and frames.",
>             parameterIds);
>     const variablePrefix = archSide == "RIGHT" ? "nv200_cabinet" : "nv200";
>     if (archSide == "LEFT")
>         wheelArchFrame(context,id+"left",name,variablePrefix,x+d.wallThickness,y,length,height,false,d);
>     else
>         benchWall(context, id+"left", name ~ (archSide == "RIGHT" ? " aisle side" : " wall side"),
>             vector(x,y,zero),vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),length,height,longBays,
>             archSide == "RIGHT" && rightAccess,d,parameterIds);
>     if (archSide == "RIGHT")
>         wheelArchFrame(context,id+"right",name,variablePrefix,x+width-total,y,length,height,true,d);
>     else
>         benchWall(context, id+"right", name ~ " aisle side", vector(x+width,y+length,zero),
>             vector(0,-1,0), vector(-1,0,0), length,height,longBays,rightAccess,d,parameterIds);
>     const setback = max(total,d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance);
>     const rearLeft = archSide == "LEFT" ? setback : leftInset;
>     const rearRight = archSide == "RIGHT" ? setback : rightInset;
>     benchWall(context, id+"rear", name ~ " rear end", vector(x+width-rearRight,y,zero),
>         vector(-1,0,0), vector(0,1,0), width-rearLeft-rearRight,height,1,false,d,parameterIds);
>     benchWall(context, id+"front", name ~ " cab end", vector(x+leftInset,y+length,zero),
>         vector(1,0,0), vector(0,-1,0), width-leftInset-rightInset,height,1,false,d,parameterIds);
> }
>
> /** Shared dimensions for the sliding comb; invalid travel is rejected rather than resizing parts. */
> function longSlatDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {
>     const f = d.frameThickness;
>     const wallInner = d.wallThickness+f;
>     const fixedInner = d.seatWidth-f;
>     const closedWidth = d.seatWidth+f;
>     const travel = d.bedWidth-closedWidth;
>     const stripClosed = fixedInner-d.slidingStripWidth-travel;
>     const setback = max(wallInner,d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance);
>     const stripRear = setback+d.stripEndClearance;
>     const stripFront = d.seatLength-wallInner-d.stripEndClearance;
>     const pitch = d.slatWidth+d.slatSideGap;
>     var count = floor((d.seatLength-d.slatSideGap)/pitch);
>     if (count % 2 == 0) count -= 1;
>     const margin = (d.seatLength-(count*d.slatWidth+(count-1)*d.slatSideGap))/2;
>     if (travel <= 0*millimeter || stripClosed < wallInner+d.slatSideGap-0.00001*millimeter)
>         throw regenError("The inner strip cannot retract between the fixed frames. Reduce bed width or strip width, or increase fixed bench width.",
>             ["seatWidth","bedWidth","frameThickness","wallThickness","slidingStripWidth","slatSideGap"]);
>     if (count < 3 || count > 101)
>         throw regenError("Long bench must accommodate between 3 and 101 interleaving slats.",
>             ["seatLength","slatWidth","slatSideGap"]);
>     if (d.stripEndClearance >= d.ledgeWidth || setback+d.ledgeWidth >= d.seatLength-wallInner-d.ledgeWidth)
>         throw regenError("Ledges need positive strip bearing and clear space between them.",
>             ["ledgeWidth","stripEndClearance","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance"]);
>     for (var i = 0; i < count; i += 2)
>     {
>         const slatY = margin+i*pitch;
>         if (slatY < setback && slatY >= wallInner)
>             throw regenError("A shortened rear slat misses the rear end support. Adjust slat width, side clearance or bench length.",
>                 ["slatWidth","slatSideGap","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance"]);
>     }
>     const firstMoving = margin+pitch;
>     const lastMoving = margin+(count-2)*pitch;
>     if (firstMoving+d.slatWidth <= stripRear || lastMoving >= stripFront)
>         throw regenError("The end moving slats must overlap the inner strip. Adjust slat spacing or rear corner setback.",
>             ["slatWidth","slatSideGap","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance","stripEndClearance"]);
>     if (d.frameThickness*2 > d.memberWidth || d.platformHeight-d.slatThickness-2*f <= d.archHeight)
>         throw regenError("Strip and ledges need room within the top band and above the wheel arch.",
>             ["frameThickness","memberWidth","platformHeight","slatThickness","archHeight"]);
>     return {
>         "count":count,"margin":margin,"pitch":pitch,"travel":travel,"closedWidth":closedWidth,
>         "wallInner":wallInner,"fixedInner":fixedInner,"stripClosed":stripClosed,
>         "stripRear":stripRear,"stripFront":stripFront,"rearLedge":setback
>     };
> }
>
> /** Separate fixed and moving slats, a copied aisle frame, an inner stop strip and two fixed ledges. */
> function longitudinalSlats(context is Context, id is Id, d is map)
> {
>     const p = longSlatDimensions(d);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const f = d.frameThickness;
>     const h = d.platformHeight-d.slatThickness;
>     const shift = d.layout == NV200Layout.NIGHT ? p.travel : zero;
>     const wood = color(0.72,0.52,0.32);
>     const movingWood = color(0.87,0.70,0.43);
>     for (var i = 0; i < p.count; i += 1)
>     {
>         const y = p.margin+i*p.pitch;
>         const moving = i % 2 == 1;
>         const start = moving ? p.stripClosed+shift :
>             (y < p.rearLedge ? p.rearLedge : d.wallThickness);
>         const end = moving ? p.closedWidth+shift : d.seatWidth;
>         makeBlock(context,id+(moving ? "movingSlat" ~ i : "fixedSlat" ~ i),
>             (moving ? "Long bench moving slat " : "Long bench fixed slat ") ~ (i+1),
>             vector(start,y,h),vector(end,y+d.slatWidth,d.platformHeight),moving ? movingWood : wood);
>     }
>     benchWall(context,id+"movingFrame","Long bench moving aisle support",
>         vector(p.closedWidth+shift,d.seatLength,zero),vector(0,-1,0),vector(-1,0,0),
>         d.seatLength,h,2,true,d,
>         ["seatLength","platformHeight","slatThickness","memberWidth","insideRadius","frameThickness"]);
>     makeBlock(context,id+"innerStrip","Long bench moving inner tie / extension stop",
>         vector(p.stripClosed+shift,p.stripRear,h-f),
>         vector(p.stripClosed+shift+d.slidingStripWidth,p.stripFront,h),movingWood);
>     // Rear ledge is inset to the corner setback, joining the retained wall post and fixed aisle frame.
>     makeBlock(context,id+"rearLedge","Long bench fixed rear inset guide ledge",
>         vector(p.wallInner,p.rearLedge,h-2*f),
>         vector(p.fixedInner,p.rearLedge+d.ledgeWidth,h-f),wood);
>     makeBlock(context,id+"frontLedge","Long bench fixed cab-end guide ledge",
>         vector(p.wallInner,d.seatLength-p.wallInner-d.ledgeWidth,h-2*f),
>         vector(p.fixedInner,d.seatLength-p.wallInner,h-f),wood);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlatCount",p.count);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlideTravel",p.travel);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlidePosition",shift);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longBenchClosedWidth",p.closedWidth);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longBenchCurrentWidth",p.closedWidth+shift);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longStripClosedClearance",p.stripClosed-p.wallInner);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlatGap",d.slatSideGap);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longFixedSlatGap",d.slatWidth+2*d.slatSideGap);
> }
>
> annotation {
>     "Feature Type Name" : "NV200Interior",
>     "Feature Type Description" : "Plywood bench carcasses with editable wall, frame and member dimensions. " ~
>         "Platform height is the top of the slats, below the foam. Long bench has two vertical access openings. " ~
>         "Layout moves the longitudinal slats and their outer support frame. Cross top, joints and toilet deployment remain undetailed."
> }
> export const nv200Interior = defineFeature(function(context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
>     precondition
>     {
>         annotation { "Name" : "Layout", "Default" : NV200Layout.DAY }
>         definition.layout is NV200Layout;
>         annotation { "Name" : "Show cushions", "Default" : true,
>             "Description" : "Include all seat and backrest cushions in the selected layout. Turn off to work on the structure." }
>         definition.showCushions is boolean;
>         annotation { "Name" : "Platform height", "Description" : "Floor to top of slats; foam sits above this." }
>         isLength(definition.platformHeight, { (meter) : [0.1, 0.4, 2], (millimeter) : 400 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>         annotation { "Group Name" : "Plywood bench construction", "Collapsed By Default" : false }

**The workable proposal is a 12 mm birch tray on the 53 mm runners, supported by two fixed longitudinal mounting frames. I’d allow a 600 mm fixed bench width—30 mm wider than the current baseline—to accommodate your crate and practical clearances.**

The load calculations support keeping the 12 mm bottom. The details needing the most attention are the joints, runner attachments and anchoring of the fixed frames.

**Proposed dimensions**

These are dimensions for the next design pass; the wheel-arch measurements remain provisional.

| Component | Proposed dimension | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Tray length | 1,200 mm | Matches shortlisted runners; final positioning must accommodate locking levers |
| Tray external width | 376 mm | Gives 352 mm inside with 12 mm sides |
| Tray bottom | 12 mm birch, flush underneath | Preserves storage height |
| Full-height front and back | 290 mm overall tray height | Clears the existing 322 mm-high opening |
| Long sides | 12 mm birch, U-shaped | Retains aisle access |
| Continuous lower band on moving sides | **90 mm high** | Accommodates the 53 mm slide with 18.5 mm above and below its envelope |
| End uprights on moving sides | 60 mm wide | Retains our established member width as a starting geometry |
| Clearance beneath tray | 10 mm | Proposed allowance for floor irregularity and movement |
| New wheel-arch-side mounting frame | **18 mm ply, approximately 300 mm high** | Provides a continuous runner mounting structure while clearing the sliding bed mechanism |

The **90 mm band is a mounting allowance**, subject to the actual runner-hole layout. The supplier’s instructions specify the slide size, **19 ±0.5 mm side clearance** and M5 fixings, but don’t provide a complete dimensioned drilling schedule. [Instant Panel instructions](https://instantpanel.co.nz/productfiles/drawer_slides/Drawer_slides_2053_Installation_Precautions_and_Instructions.pdf)

**Width and height**

Across the van, the proposed arrangement is:

| Width allocation | mm |
|---|---:|
| Provisional wheel-arch intrusion | 140 |
| Arch-to-frame clearance | 10 |
| New fixed frame | 18 |
| Two runners | 38 |
| Two drawer sides | 24 |
| Clear drawer interior | 352 |
| Existing aisle frame | 18 |
| **Fixed bench width** | **600** |

The 330 mm crate then has **22 mm total spare width**, some of which must accommodate any projecting fasteners. At the current 570 mm bench width, this arrangement provides only 322 mm internally.

The additional 18 mm moving bed frame makes the closed bench **618 mm wide**, leaving **452 mm of daytime aisle** to the cabinet. The nighttime bed can remain 1,070 mm wide by reducing its extension travel accordingly.

Vertically:

**10 mm floor clearance + 12 mm bottom + 267 mm container = 289 mm.**

That leaves **33 mm beneath the existing 322 mm opening**. The proposed tray end panels reach 300 mm above the floor, leaving 22 mm clearance themselves. There is no raised groove consuming additional storage height.

**The fixed mounting frames**

The new frame beside the arch needs a **continuous lower rail**, with end posts and a middle post connecting it to an upper rail. I propose:

- An approximately **100 mm-high lower mounting rail**.
- Our existing **60 mm posts and upper rail**.
- Approximately **300 mm overall height**.
- Attachment to the fixed bench structure, including connections that resist upward pull.

The aisle-side runner also needs a continuous mounting rail. We should incorporate that into the existing **18 mm frame plane**, retaining its access openings above it. Adding another layer inside would consume more drawer width.

The new arch-side frame must stay below the bed’s moving tie strip. In the current source geometry, that strip’s underside is at **364 mm**, and the fixed guide ledges reach down to **346 mm**. A 300 mm frame clears both.

The rear drawer opening also needs redesigning: the existing rear panel and its uprights obstruct the proposed drawer. The rear slat still needs its fixed supporting header.

**Load check**

I used **40 kg total drawer-plus-contents** as a proposed working-load case and checked the bottom again at the runners’ published **61 kg distributed-load rating**.

The bottom spans approximately **352 mm between the long sides**. Using a simple supported-strip calculation and a birch stiffness assumption of 6,500 N/mm²:

| Load case | Calculated bottom bending stress | Calculated bottom deflection |
|---|---:|---:|
| 40 kg spread over the bottom | About 0.6 MPa | About 0.2 mm |
| 61 kg spread over the bottom | About 0.9 MPa | About 0.3 mm |
| 20 kg concentrated centrally across a 460 mm-long section | About 1.6 MPa | About 0.4 mm |

The stiffness assumption is slightly below the weaker-direction value published for 12 mm, nine-ply sanded Riga birch. These calculations assume sound, continuously supported edges and exclude joint movement. They give good reason to retain the **12 mm bottom without adding crossbars underneath**. [Riga plywood handbook, Table 4.9](https://www.finieris.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/RigaWood_PlywoodHandbook.pdf)

**The extended drawer creates an overturning load.** With 40 kg evenly distributed and its centre roughly 600 mm beyond the rear support, the moment is about **235 N·m**. For fixed attachments spaced 1,200 mm apart, the simplified reactions across both sides are approximately:

- **589 N downward at the rear**, equivalent to 60 kg weight.
- **196 N upward at the cab end**, equivalent to 20 kg weight.

At 61 kg, those become approximately 898 N downward and 299 N upward. This is why the new frame needs positive attachment at both ends; resting it on the floor is insufficient. Exact anchor sizes depend on the actual bench-to-vehicle connections, which remain unspecified.

**Bottom joints and runner fixings**

For the agreed flush, glued-and-screwed bottom, I recommend a **continuous epoxy bond** along both sides and both ends, following the adhesive manufacturer’s wet-out and thickened-bonding procedure. That preserves the flat underside. [WEST SYSTEM bonding instructions](https://www.westsystem.com/instruction/epoxy-basics/bonding-and-clamping/)

The screws can hold the assembly together during curing. I found no defensible published structural screw schedule for this particular 12 mm plywood-edge joint, so I cannot assign it a capacity from screw count alone. APA’s published edge-fastening tests use thicker plywood. [APA fastener guidance](https://www.apawood.org/guides-tools-training/technical-document-library/technical-notes/fastener-loads-for-plywood-screws/)

For the runners, **M5 through-fixings through the plywood faces** are the preferred arrangement where head and nut clearances permit. Their positions must follow the actual slides.

**My recommendation is to develop this 600 mm-wide arrangement, retaining the 12 mm flush-bottom tray and a 300 mm-high internal mounting frame.** The remaining checks are the runner drilling pattern and lever clearance, the fixed-frame anchors, and a loaded trial of the completed glued tray. Those checks determine the finished assembly’s usable load rating.

> function nameAndColor(context is Context, bodies is Query, name is string, appearance is Color)
> {
>     setProperty(context, { "entities" : bodies, "propertyType" : PropertyType.NAME, "value" : name });
>     setProperty(context, { "entities" : bodies, "propertyType" : PropertyType.APPEARANCE, "value" : appearance });
> }
>
> function makeBlock(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, lo is Vector, hi is Vector, appearance is Color)
> {
>     fCuboid(context, id, { "corner1" : lo, "corner2" : hi });
>     nameAndColor(context, qCreatedBy(id, EntityType.BODY), name, appearance);
> }
>
> function footprintSketch(context is Context, id is Id, points is array)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id, {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(vector(0, 0, 0) * centimeter, vector(0, 0, 1), vector(1, 0, 0))
>     });
>     skPolyline(sketch, "outline", { "points" : points });
>     skSolve(sketch);
> }
>
> /** Rounded opening cutter in the vertical plane of a plywood panel. */
> function openingTool(context is Context, id is Id, origin is Vector, along is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, x0, x1, bottom, top, radius, depth)
> {
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context, id + "sketch", {
>         "sketchPlane" : plane(origin, normal, along)
>     });
>     const r = radius;
>     const k = 1 - 1 / sqrt(2);
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "bottom", { "start" : vector(x0+r,bottom), "end" : vector(x1-r,bottom) });
>     skArc(sketch, "br", { "start" : vector(x1-r,bottom),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x1,bottom+r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "right", { "start" : vector(x1,bottom+r), "end" : vector(x1,top-r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tr", { "start" : vector(x1,top-r),
>         "mid" : vector(x1-k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x1-r,top) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "top", { "start" : vector(x1-r,top), "end" : vector(x0+r,top) });
>     skArc(sketch, "tl", { "start" : vector(x0+r,top),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,top-k*r), "end" : vector(x0,top-r) });
>     skLineSegment(sketch, "left", { "start" : vector(x0,top-r), "end" : vector(x0,bottom+r) });
>     skArc(sketch, "bl", { "start" : vector(x0,bottom+r),
>         "mid" : vector(x0+k*r,bottom+k*r), "end" : vector(x0+r,bottom) });
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context, id + "solid", { "entities" : qSketchRegion(id + "sketch"),
>         "direction" : normal, "endBound" : BoundingType.BLIND, "endDepth" : depth });
>     opDeleteBodies(context, id + "cleanup", { "entities" : qCreatedBy(id + "sketch", EntityType.BODY) });
> }
>
> /** Access faces use an open-bottom frame only; closed faces also retain a solid outer skin. */
> function benchWall(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     along is Vector, normal is Vector, length, height, bays is number, access is boolean, d is map, parameterIds is array)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const r = d.insideRadius;
>     const bay = (length - (bays + 1) * w) / bays;
>     if (bay <= 2*r || height <= 2*w + 2*r)
>         throw regenError("Panel is too small for its bands, posts and corner radii.",
>             parameterIds);
>     const up = vector(0,0,1);
>     for (var layer = access ? 1 : 0; layer < 2; layer += 1)
>     {
>         const layerId = id + ("layer" ~ layer);
>         const offset = layer == 0 || access ? 0*millimeter : d.wallThickness;
>         const thickness = layer == 0 ? d.wallThickness : d.frameThickness;
>         const start = origin + normal*offset;
>         fCuboid(context, layerId + "plate", {
>             "corner1" : start,
>             "corner2" : start + along*length + normal*thickness + up*height
>         });
>         const plate = qCreatedBy(layerId + "plate", EntityType.BODY);
>         if (layer == 1)
>         {
>             for (var i = 0; i < bays; i += 1)
>             {
>                 const cutId = layerId + ("opening" ~ i);
>                 const left = w + i*(bay+w);
>                 // All frame openings reach the floor; no cut-out outer skins are generated.
>                 const bottom = -2*r;
>                 openingTool(context, cutId, start - normal*millimeter, along, normal,
>                     left, left+bay, bottom, height-w, r, thickness+2*millimeter);
>                 opBoolean(context, cutId + "subtract", {
>                     "tools" : qCreatedBy(cutId + "solid", EntityType.BODY),
>                     "targets" : plate, "operationType" : BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>                 });
>             }
>         }
>         nameAndColor(context, plate, name ~ (layer == 0 ? " - outer wall" : " - inner frame"),
>             layer == 0 ? color(0.75,0.66,0.49) : color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     }
> }
>
>
>
>
> /** Door reference outlines only; rectangles do not imply body contours, door leaves or travel paths. */
> function doorOutline(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, origin is Vector,
>     normal is Vector, along is Vector, width, height)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id,{"sketchPlane":plane(origin,normal,along)});
>     const corners = [vector(zero,zero),vector(width,zero),vector(width,height),vector(zero,height)];
>     for (var i = 0; i < 4; i += 1)
>         skLineSegment(sketch,"edge" ~ i,{"start":corners[i],"end":corners[(i+1)%4],"construction":true});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     setProperty(context,{"entities":qCreatedBy(id,EntityType.BODY),"propertyType":PropertyType.NAME,"value":name});
> }
>
> /** Rounded upper ends only: editable visual approximation, with the full base footprint retained. */
> function wheelArchReference(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, depth, d is map)
> {
>     const r = d.archRadius;
>     const length = d.archLength;
>     const height = d.archHeight;
>     if (r <= 0*millimeter || 2*r >= length || r >= height)
>         throw regenError("Arch rounding radius must be positive, below its height and below half its length.",
>             ["archRadius", "archLength", "archHeight"]);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const k = 1-1/sqrt(2);
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id+"profile",{
>         "sketchPlane":plane(vector(x,d.archRearOffset,zero),vector(1,0,0),vector(0,1,0))
>     });
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"base",{"start":vector(zero,zero),"end":vector(length,zero)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"front",{"start":vector(length,zero),"end":vector(length,height-r)});
>     skArc(sketch,"frontRound",{"start":vector(length,height-r),
>         "mid":vector(length-k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(length-r,height)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"top",{"start":vector(length-r,height),"end":vector(r,height)});
>     skArc(sketch,"rearRound",{"start":vector(r,height),
>         "mid":vector(k*r,height-k*r),"end":vector(zero,height-r)});
>     skLineSegment(sketch,"rear",{"start":vector(zero,height-r),"end":vector(zero,zero)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"body",{"entities":qSketchRegion(id+"profile"),"direction":vector(1,0,0),
>         "endBound":BoundingType.BLIND,"endDepth":depth});
>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"body",EntityType.BODY),name,color(0.45,0.49,0.52));
> }
>
>
> /** Concave rear body corner surface. Radius is provisional; height follows the rear opening reference. */
> function rearCornerReference(context is Context, id is Id, right is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const r = d.rearCornerRadius;
>     const k = 1-1/sqrt(2);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const x = right ? d.cargoWidth : zero;
>     const sign = right ? -1 : 1;
>     const sketch = newSketchOnPlane(context,id+"profile",{
>         "sketchPlane":plane(vector(zero,zero,zero),vector(0,0,1),vector(1,0,0))
>     });
>     skArc(sketch,"corner",{"start":vector(x+sign*r,zero),
>         "mid":vector(x+sign*k*r,k*r),"end":vector(x,r)});
>     skSolve(sketch);
>     opExtrude(context,id+"surface",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.EDGE),
>         "direction":vector(0,0,1),"endBound":BoundingType.BLIND,
>         "endDepth":d.rearDoorSill+d.rearDoorHeight});
>     opDeleteBodies(context,id+"cleanup",{"entities":qCreatedBy(id+"profile",EntityType.BODY)});
>     nameAndColor(context,qCreatedBy(id+"surface",EntityType.BODY),
>         (right ? "Right" : "Left") ~ " rear body corner - approximate surface",color(0.55,0.58,0.61));
> }
>
> /** Frame only along the long bench wall: broad rear end, one post after the arch, front end. */
> function wheelArchFrame(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, variablePrefix is string,
>     frameX, y, length, height, combineFrontPosts is boolean, d is map)
> {
>     const w = d.memberWidth;
>     const parameterIds = variablePrefix == "nv200_cabinet" ?
>         ["cabinetHeight", "cabinetOuterLength", "memberWidth", "insideRadius",
>          "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archHeight", "archClearance", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"] :
>         ["platformHeight", "slatThickness", "seatLength", "memberWidth", "insideRadius",
>          "archRearOffset", "archLength", "archHeight", "archClearance", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"];
>     const setback = d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance;
>     const rearSupportEnd = max(d.archRearOffset-d.archClearance,setback+w);
>     const rearClearance = d.archRearOffset-rearSupportEnd;
>     if (rearClearance <= 0*millimeter)
>         throw regenError("Rear corner setback and post reach the wheel arch. Check measured dimensions.", parameterIds);
>     const archFront = d.archRearOffset+d.archLength;
>     // Adjacent uprights retain both member widths: 60 + 60 = 120 mm at baseline.
>     const postWidth = combineFrontPosts ? 2*w : w;
>     const postStart = combineFrontPosts ? length-postWidth : archFront+d.archClearance;
>     const postEnd = postStart+postWidth;
>     const frontClearance = postStart-archFront;
>     if (rearSupportEnd < w || frontClearance < d.archClearance ||
>         (!combineFrontPosts && postEnd > length-w))
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch and clearances leave insufficient room for the wall-side supports.", parameterIds);
>     if (d.archHeight > height-w)
>         throw regenError("Wheel arch reaches above the underside of the wall-side top band.", parameterIds);
>     const origin = vector(frameX,y+setback,0*millimeter);
>     // Retain the inner-frame plane so it meets the existing end panels.
>     fCuboid(context, id+"plate", {
>         "corner1" : origin,
>         "corner2" : origin+vector(d.frameThickness,length-setback,height)
>     });
>     const frame = qCreatedBy(id+"plate",EntityType.BODY);
>     const openings = combineFrontPosts ? [[rearSupportEnd,postStart]] : [[rearSupportEnd,postStart],[postEnd,length-w]];
>     for (var i = 0; i < size(openings); i += 1)
>     {
>         const bounds = openings[i];
>         const gap = bounds[1]-bounds[0];
>         if (gap > 0*millimeter)
>         {
>             const radius = d.insideRadius;
>             if (gap <= 2*radius || height-w <= 2*radius)
>                 throw regenError("Wall-side opening is too small for the specified corner radius.", parameterIds);
>             const endClearance = min(rearClearance,frontClearance);
>             if (i == 0 && endClearance < radius)
>             {
>                 const cornerHeight = height-w-radius+
>                     sqrt(radius^2-(radius-endClearance)^2);
>                 if (d.archHeight > cornerHeight)
>                     throw regenError("Wheel arch intersects the rounded opening corners.", parameterIds);
>             }
>             const cutId = id+("opening" ~ i);
>             openingTool(context,cutId,origin-vector(1,0,0)*millimeter,
>                 vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),bounds[0]-setback,bounds[1]-setback,-2*radius,height-w,
>                 radius,d.frameThickness+2*millimeter);
>             opBoolean(context,cutId+"subtract",{
>                 "tools":qCreatedBy(cutId+"solid",EntityType.BODY),
>                 "targets":frame,"operationType":BooleanOperationType.SUBTRACTION
>             });
>         }
>     }
>     nameAndColor(context,frame,name ~ " wall-side frame - wheel-arch opening",color(0.88,0.61,0.25));
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportWidth",rearSupportEnd-setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportStart",y+setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearWallSupportEnd",y+rearSupportEnd);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearArchClearance",rearClearance);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_frontArchClearance",frontClearance);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_rearCornerSetback",setback);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_wallPostStart",y+postStart);
>     setVariable(context,variablePrefix ~ "_wallPostEnd",y+postEnd);
> }
>
> /** End walls fit the actual side build-ups: exposed frames sit at the nominal aisle boundary. */
> function benchCarcass(context is Context, id is Id, name is string, x, y, width, length,
>     height, longBays is number, rightAccess is boolean, archSide is string, d is map)
> {
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const parameterIds = archSide == "RIGHT" ?
>         ["wallThickness", "frameThickness", "memberWidth", "insideRadius", "cabinetHeight",
>          "cabinetOuterLength", "cargoWidth", "bedWidth", "rearCornerRadius", "rearCornerAllowance"] :
>         ["wallThickness", "frameThickness", "memberWidth", "insideRadius", "platformHeight",
>          "slatThickness", "seatWidth", "seatLength", "cargoLength", "crossExtension"];
>     const total = d.wallThickness+d.frameThickness;
>     const leftInset = archSide == "RIGHT" && rightAccess ? d.frameThickness : total;
>     const rightInset = archSide != "RIGHT" && rightAccess ? d.frameThickness : total;
>     if (width <= leftInset+rightInset || length <= 2*total)
>         throw regenError("Carcass width and length must leave room between opposing walls and frames.",
>             parameterIds);
>     const variablePrefix = archSide == "RIGHT" ? "nv200_cabinet" : "nv200";
>     if (archSide == "LEFT")
>         wheelArchFrame(context,id+"left",name,variablePrefix,x+d.wallThickness,y,length,height,false,d);
>     else
>         benchWall(context, id+"left", name ~ (archSide == "RIGHT" ? " aisle side" : " wall side"),
>             vector(x,y,zero),vector(0,1,0),vector(1,0,0),length,height,longBays,
>             archSide == "RIGHT" && rightAccess,d,parameterIds);
>     if (archSide == "RIGHT")
>         wheelArchFrame(context,id+"right",name,variablePrefix,x+width-total,y,length,height,true,d);
>     else
>         benchWall(context, id+"right", name ~ " aisle side", vector(x+width,y+length,zero),
>             vector(0,-1,0), vector(-1,0,0), length,height,longBays,rightAccess,d,parameterIds);
>     const setback = max(total,d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance);
>     const rearLeft = archSide == "LEFT" ? setback : leftInset;
>     const rearRight = archSide == "RIGHT" ? setback : rightInset;
>     benchWall(context, id+"rear", name ~ " rear end", vector(x+width-rearRight,y,zero),
>         vector(-1,0,0), vector(0,1,0), width-rearLeft-rearRight,height,1,false,d,parameterIds);
>     benchWall(context, id+"front", name ~ " cab end", vector(x+leftInset,y+length,zero),
>         vector(1,0,0), vector(0,-1,0), width-leftInset-rightInset,height,1,false,d,parameterIds);
> }
>
> /** Shared dimensions for the sliding comb; invalid travel is rejected rather than resizing parts. */
> function longSlatDimensions(d is map) returns map
> {
>     const f = d.frameThickness;
>     const wallInner = d.wallThickness+f;
>     const fixedInner = d.seatWidth-f;
>     const closedWidth = d.seatWidth+f;
>     const travel = d.bedWidth-closedWidth;
>     const stripClosed = fixedInner-d.slidingStripWidth-travel;
>     const setback = max(wallInner,d.rearCornerRadius+d.rearCornerAllowance);
>     const stripRear = setback+d.stripEndClearance;
>     const stripFront = d.seatLength-wallInner-d.stripEndClearance;
>     const pitch = d.slatWidth+d.slatSideGap;
>     var count = floor((d.seatLength-d.slatSideGap)/pitch);
>     if (count % 2 == 0) count -= 1;
>     const margin = (d.seatLength-(count*d.slatWidth+(count-1)*d.slatSideGap))/2;
>     if (travel <= 0*millimeter || stripClosed < wallInner+d.slatSideGap-0.00001*millimeter)
>         throw regenError("The inner strip cannot retract between the fixed frames. Reduce bed width or strip width, or increase fixed bench width.",
>             ["seatWidth","bedWidth","frameThickness","wallThickness","slidingStripWidth","slatSideGap"]);
>     if (count < 3 || count > 101)
>         throw regenError("Long bench must accommodate between 3 and 101 interleaving slats.",
>             ["seatLength","slatWidth","slatSideGap"]);
>     if (d.stripEndClearance >= d.ledgeWidth || setback+d.ledgeWidth >= d.seatLength-wallInner-d.ledgeWidth)
>         throw regenError("Ledges need positive strip bearing and clear space between them.",
>             ["ledgeWidth","stripEndClearance","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance"]);
>     for (var i = 0; i < count; i += 2)
>     {
>         const slatY = margin+i*pitch;
>         if (slatY < setback && slatY >= wallInner)
>             throw regenError("A shortened rear slat misses the rear end support. Adjust slat width, side clearance or bench length.",
>                 ["slatWidth","slatSideGap","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance"]);
>     }
>     const firstMoving = margin+pitch;
>     const lastMoving = margin+(count-2)*pitch;
>     if (firstMoving+d.slatWidth <= stripRear || lastMoving >= stripFront)
>         throw regenError("The end moving slats must overlap the inner strip. Adjust slat spacing or rear corner setback.",
>             ["slatWidth","slatSideGap","seatLength","rearCornerRadius","rearCornerAllowance","stripEndClearance"]);
>     if (d.frameThickness*2 > d.memberWidth || d.platformHeight-d.slatThickness-2*f <= d.archHeight)
>         throw regenError("Strip and ledges need room within the top band and above the wheel arch.",
>             ["frameThickness","memberWidth","platformHeight","slatThickness","archHeight"]);
>     return {
>         "count":count,"margin":margin,"pitch":pitch,"travel":travel,"closedWidth":closedWidth,
>         "wallInner":wallInner,"fixedInner":fixedInner,"stripClosed":stripClosed,
>         "stripRear":stripRear,"stripFront":stripFront,"rearLedge":setback
>     };
> }
>
> /** Separate fixed and moving slats, a copied aisle frame, an inner stop strip and two fixed ledges. */
> function longitudinalSlats(context is Context, id is Id, d is map)
> {
>     const p = longSlatDimensions(d);
>     const zero = 0*millimeter;
>     const f = d.frameThickness;
>     const h = d.platformHeight-d.slatThickness;
>     const shift = d.layout == NV200Layout.NIGHT ? p.travel : zero;
>     const wood = color(0.72,0.52,0.32);
>     const movingWood = color(0.87,0.70,0.43);
>     for (var i = 0; i < p.count; i += 1)
>     {
>         const y = p.margin+i*p.pitch;
>         const moving = i % 2 == 1;
>         const start = moving ? p.stripClosed+shift :
>             (y < p.rearLedge ? p.rearLedge : d.wallThickness);
>         const end = moving ? p.closedWidth+shift : d.seatWidth;
>         makeBlock(context,id+(moving ? "movingSlat" ~ i : "fixedSlat" ~ i),
>             (moving ? "Long bench moving slat " : "Long bench fixed slat ") ~ (i+1),
>             vector(start,y,h),vector(end,y+d.slatWidth,d.platformHeight),moving ? movingWood : wood);
>     }
>     benchWall(context,id+"movingFrame","Long bench moving aisle support",
>         vector(p.closedWidth+shift,d.seatLength,zero),vector(0,-1,0),vector(-1,0,0),
>         d.seatLength,h,2,true,d,
>         ["seatLength","platformHeight","slatThickness","memberWidth","insideRadius","frameThickness"]);
>     makeBlock(context,id+"innerStrip","Long bench moving inner tie / extension stop",
>         vector(p.stripClosed+shift,p.stripRear,h-f),
>         vector(p.stripClosed+shift+d.slidingStripWidth,p.stripFront,h),movingWood);
>     // Rear ledge is inset to the corner setback, joining the retained wall post and fixed aisle frame.
>     makeBlock(context,id+"rearLedge","Long bench fixed rear inset guide ledge",
>         vector(p.wallInner,p.rearLedge,h-2*f),
>         vector(p.fixedInner,p.rearLedge+d.ledgeWidth,h-f),wood);
>     makeBlock(context,id+"frontLedge","Long bench fixed cab-end guide ledge",
>         vector(p.wallInner,d.seatLength-p.wallInner-d.ledgeWidth,h-2*f),
>         vector(p.fixedInner,d.seatLength-p.wallInner,h-f),wood);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlatCount",p.count);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlideTravel",p.travel);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlidePosition",shift);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longBenchClosedWidth",p.closedWidth);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longBenchCurrentWidth",p.closedWidth+shift);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longStripClosedClearance",p.stripClosed-p.wallInner);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longSlatGap",d.slatSideGap);
>     setVariable(context,"nv200_longFixedSlatGap",d.slatWidth+2*d.slatSideGap);
> }
>
> annotation {
>     "Feature Type Name" : "NV200Interior",
>     "Feature Type Description" : "Plywood bench carcasses with editable wall, frame and member dimensions. " ~
>         "Platform height is the top of the slats, below the foam. Long bench has two vertical access openings. " ~
>         "Layout moves the longitudinal slats and their outer support frame. Cross top, joints and toilet deployment remain undetailed."
> }
> export const nv200Interior = defineFeature(function(context is Context, id is Id, definition is map)
>     precondition
>     {
>         annotation { "Name" : "Layout", "Default" : NV200Layout.DAY }
>         definition.layout is NV200Layout;
>         annotation { "Name" : "Show cushions", "Default" : true,
>             "Description" : "Include all seat and backrest cushions in the selected layout. Turn off to work on the structure." }
>         definition.showCushions is boolean;
>         annotation { "Name" : "Platform height", "Description" : "Floor to top of slats; foam sits above this." }
>         isLength(definition.platformHeight, { (meter) : [0.1, 0.4, 2], (millimeter) : 400 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>         annotation { "Group Name" : "Plywood bench construction", "Collapsed By Default" : false }
>         {
>             annotation { "Name" : "Outer wall thickness" }
>             isLength(definition.wallThickness, { (meter) : [0.001, 0.007, 0.05], (millimeter) : 7 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>             annotation { "Name" : "Inner frame thickness" }
>             isLength(definition.frameThickness, { (meter) : [0.001, 0.018, 0.1], (millimeter) : 18 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>             annotation { "Name" : "Beam and post width" }
>             isLength(definition.memberWidth, { (meter) : [0.01, 0.06, 0.3], (millimeter) : 60 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>             annotation { "Name" : "Inside corner radius" }
>             isLength(definition.insideRadius, { (meter) : [0.001, 0.025, 0.2], (millimeter) : 25 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>             annotation { "Name" : "Slat thickness", "Description" : "Timber slat thickness; top remains at platform height." }
>             isLength(definition.slatThickness, { (meter) : [0.001, 0.018, 0.1], (millimeter) : 18 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>             annotation { "Name" : "Cross bench extension", "Description" : "Fixed cross bench width = bed width minus extension." }
>             isLength(definition.crossExtension, { (meter) : [0.001, 0.2, 0.7], (millimeter) : 200 } as LengthBoundSpec);
>         }
>         annotation { "Group Name" : "Long bench sliding slats", "Collapsed By Default" : false }
>         {
>             annotation { "Name" : "Slat width" }
>             isLength(definition.slatWidth, { (meter) : [0.01,0.08,0.3], (millimeter) : 80 } as LengthBoundSpec);

> ```text
> FeatureScript 3095 modelling notes (2026-10-14):
> - Feature Id addition is hierarchical: qCreatedBy(id+"wall"+"layer"+"plate") is different from qCreatedBy(id+"walllayerplate"). Test queries must use the same component path as production.
> - After invoking a defineFeature, its Id scope is finalized. In evaluator tests, cleanup operations must use a separate sibling Id (e.g. makeId("cleanup0")), not a child of the completed feature Id.
> - In test_featurescript, the second lambda argument is a queries map, even though the tool examples call it id. For geometry operations inside the evaluation lambda, create an Id explicitly with makeId("probe"). Adding a string to the second argument fails with 'Can not add map and string'.
> - 'box' is reserved syntax; do not name a helper function box. Renaming it makeBlock fixed a 'no features found' compilation failure.
> - A zero-thickness footprint can be made with newSketchOnPlane, skPolyline, skSolve, then opExtractSurface with faces:qSketchRegion(sketchId) and offset:0*centimeter. qCreatedBy(surfaceId,EntityType.BODY) resolves the resulting surface.
> - qBodyType(...,BodyType.SHEET) includes sketch region bodies. Use qSketchFilter(query,SketchObject.NO) when counting actual surface parts.
> - test_feature invokes the first exported feature. Place a self-contained validation feature before the production feature when testing both together. Exact geometry bounds and volumes can be checked with evBox3d(...tight:true) and evVolume; assert failures surface as notices, sometimes INFO, so inspect messages rather than relying on isError alone.
> ```
